- **Default environment.** A new task and the review of a new workflow start in this environment. You still choose the environment of a single workflow or task yourself.
- **Approvals and notifications.** Both are described in “Notifications and quiet hours”.

### Two of us: one builds, one approves

With this answer, every workflow approval in the workspace needs two different people. The first person approves, the approval waits, and only the approval of a second person who may approve lets the workflow run. Nobody can approve alone, also not in chat or through a task.

- Only an administrator switches this on. If you are not one, you read that an administrator has to switch it on.
- It needs at least two people who may approve. If the named person has not joined yet, two-person approval starts by itself once they have joined.
- A waiting approval ends after 72 hours. It also ends when the workflow changes before the second approval.
- Choosing **Me** later does not switch two-person approval off. Only an administrator switches it off again, and that is recorded in the audit log.

“Reference: pair approval, invitations, offline reports and notification pause” lists the routes and states.

### Change answers later

1. Open **Settings** and, in it, **Setup**.
2. Select **Change** on the answer you want to change.
3. Choose the new answer and then **Apply**. You read “Setting applied”.

Each change applies right away to the setting named.

When SubKit asks before a step is not a setup answer. Your request and your rules decide it; “When SubKit asks” explains how, including the rule **Always ask first**.

The overview of **Settings** shows your choice in one line, for example “Test first · Right away”.

### Good to know

- The answers belong to you, not to the workspace. Every person sets SubKit up for themselves.
- The audit trail records every change as “Setup choices changed”.
- The recommended values are: **Test first**, **Me** and **Right away**, and for administrators **$50** as the monthly AI budget.
- If you, as an administrator, name an address that is not in the workspace yet, SubKit prepares an invitation and sends no email. The invited person joins the workspace as a member; that is why “Role: Member” is shown next to the field. This role may approve.
- If you name a person whose role may not approve, SubKit stores the choice and warns under **Settings** › **Setup**: “… cannot approve with the current role. Approval notifications stay with you until an administrator changes the role.”
- If you name an unknown address without the Administrator role, it is stored but nobody is invited. As soon as an administrator invites or adds the address, SubKit links your choice by itself; the notifications go to the person once they have joined.
- If you choose **Only during my working hours**, you enter your **Working days** besides **From** and **Until**. Monday to Friday are preset.

### If something does not work

| What you see | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| “The recommended settings were not saved” | Nothing was changed. **Continue without saving** lets you go on with the recommended settings. This browser remembers your choice; in another browser the step appears again. |
| “The setting was not applied” | Your earlier choice still applies. Try again. |
| “Your setup could not be loaded” | Select **Try again**. |
| “Enter a valid email address, for example anna@example.com.” | Check the address of the person who should approve. |
| “Choose at least one service.” | Choose a service or **Other service**. |
| The step does not appear | You already answered it or skipped it with **Not now**, or you lack `settings:write`. Your answers are under **Settings › Setup**. |

### The same over the HTTP API

`GET /v1/identity/me/setup` reads your answers. The field `unset` names what you have not chosen yet, and `recommended` the recommended values.
`PUT /v1/identity/me/setup` stores answers. Fields you leave out keep their value.

```bash
curl -s -X PUT "$SUBKIT_URL/v1/identity/me/setup" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SUBKIT_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"ask_before_writing":true,"default_environment":"dev"}'
```

Every field is listed in “Reference: desktop app, rules, schedules and problem reports”.
## When SubKit asks

This chapter is for anyone who works in chat or with tasks and wants to know when SubKit asks before a step.
Afterwards you can read and answer a question card, save a recurring action as a rule, and make SubKit ask before every step that writes.
You also know exactly under which conditions something runs without a question, and where this check has its limits.

### How SubKit decides

There is no mode you pick per conversation. Two things decide whether a step asks:

1. **Your request.** SubKit checks every step against what you asked for. When your request covers the step, it runs without a question. Otherwise the question card appears.
2. **Your rules.** A saved rule lets one recurring action run without a question. The rule **Always ask first** makes every step that writes ask, even when your request covers it.

Reading, searching and preparing drafts run without a question. Three things always apply:

- A live run of a workflow needs an approval. “Your first workflow” describes how you give it.
- Payments, deletions, publications, settings, new accounts and credentials always ask.
- What a web page, an email or a file says is never a request.

### When something runs without a question

An action runs without a question only when all of the following conditions hold. If one is missing, the question card appears.

1. **You are signed in in the browser, or it is a run of your own task.** The rule applies to you in a Cockpit session: in the browser, in the installed app or in SubKit Desktop. It also applies in a run of a task you own, when you started the run or its schedule did (see “Your request covers the whole job”). With an API key, in the `subkit` command line, from an AI client over MCP and in a task run someone else started, each of these actions asks.
2. **It is a call to a connector.** The rule applies to calls that send, create or change something through a connector, and to saving a connector draft. Tools of external MCP servers and SQL statements always ask.
3. **SubKit knows the effect, and it is ordinary.** SubKit assigns every operation an effect. Payment, deletion, publication, permissions or settings, new account and credentials always ask. So does every call with `DELETE` and every call that sets a header with credentials. When SubKit cannot tell what an operation does, it asks.
4. **You asked for it in your own words.** Your latest message contains a request such as “Send …” or “Can you create …”. An information question such as “What would happen if …” is not a request. When the request carries a condition or a “not”, SubKit asks. The verb has to match the action: “create” does not cover sending. A request to send also covers the draft that comes before it, never the other way round.
5. **The request is not in pasted text.** These do not count as your words: code blocks, quoted lines, forwarded emails, everything after a lead-in such as “Here is the email:” and pasted passages of 5 lines or 800 characters and more. What a web page, a file or a service returns is never a request.
6. **You named the target.** Every recipient, every address and every target comes from your last three messages or from your answers to questions SubKit asked. If you gave a name, SubKit may have looked up the address for it in this conversation. You also have to have stated amounts, values, dates and times. SubKit reads dates and times in the time zone of the workspace.
7. **The content is yours.** A text that goes out consists of your words, or SubKit showed it to you as a draft earlier in the conversation. With your words, SubKit may add a greeting, a closing and a few filler words: at most a quarter of the words and never more than three. A new link, a new address, a new number or a new “not” leads to the question. A text of more than 1,200 characters has to have been shown as a draft.
8. **It is the first time for this request.** A request covers each action once. Creating or changing several things on the same target runs when the content differs, for example three issues with three titles from your message. Sending to the same recipients and repeating an action with the same content asks.

One special case: when the action only creates a draft at the service, SubKit does not check the content, because nothing goes out yet.

### Your request covers the whole job

A request covers every step needed to reach its result, not only the first one. That job has a clear end:

- **In chat** the job starts with your message and ends with your next message, or 2 hours after your message. Your next message starts a new job. A request from an earlier message no longer covers anything.
- **In a task run** the job is that run, until the run's deadline. The task's goal, as you wrote it, counts as your words. That applies when you own the task and you started the run, or the task's schedule did. Your saved rules apply there too. If the task changed after the run started, the goal covers nothing. If someone else, for example an admin, last changed the goal or “Done when”, they are not your words and cover nothing until you change them yourself. The task's bound connectors and workflows stay its outer limit. A run someone else started keeps only the task's standing permission, and every write asks as before.

Inside the job, the always-ask classes still ask: payments, deletions, publications and sending to recipients you did not name, settings, new accounts and credentials. What a web page, an email or a file says never adds to the job.

When an action runs without a question, the conversation shows a line below it such as “Send to anna@example.com, because you asked for it”. **Show your words** shows the sentence SubKit relies on. The audit trail records each of these actions with the reason “The person asked for it in their own words” or “A rule the person saved covers it”.

### The question card

When SubKit asks, it shows a card titled **Your decision**.

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **Action** | What happens: Send, Create, Change, Run or Save. |
| **Target** | The operation at the service, for example `POST /v1/messages`. |
| **Account** | The connector the action goes through. |
| **Recipients** | Every address, link and handle the action reaches. |
| **Content** | The full text as it would go out. |

Below the fields the card says why SubKit asks, for example “You did not name this recipient.” The last line names the deadline and adds: “A different recipient or content asks again”. **Allow once** applies to exactly this action.

1. Read the fields, above all **Recipients** and **Content**.
2. Select **Allow once** if exactly this should happen. The action runs once.
3. Select **Decline** if not. Nothing runs.

You can keep writing while a card is open:

- **Typed text never gives an approval.** A card that lets an action run, such as **Allow once**, takes its answer from its buttons only. If you type “yes”, it reaches SubKit as an ordinary message, nothing runs, and the card stays open.
- **A plain question takes a typed answer.** A yes-or-no question with no action attached takes a clear “yes” or “no”. A question with options takes a reply that names exactly one option. Anything else reaches SubKit as an ordinary message, and the question stays open.
- **A secret goes into its form only.** While a form asks for a password or key, a typed message is refused and never stored.

### Save an action as a rule

A rule allows exactly one recurring action without a question. You do not create it by hand: SubKit offers it when you have confirmed the same action with **Allow once** for the second time.

1. Confirm the action as usual. Below the card, “Should this run without asking from now on?” appears with the **Scope** of the rule.
2. Check the scope: action, target, account and recipients.
3. Select **Save as rule**. Or select **No, keep asking**; SubKit then does not offer this rule again.

A rule applies like this:

| Property | What applies |
| --- | --- |
| Scope | Exactly this action through exactly this connector to exactly this operation. With recipients: only to the recipients named. Without recipients: only actions without a recipient. At most 20 recipients. |
| Content | If the text was the same in both confirmations, the rule covers only exactly this text. If it differed, the rule covers only text you wrote yourself or saw as a draft. If the action carried no text, it covers only actions without text. |
| Duration | 90 days from saving. After that the action asks again. |
| Daily limit | 20 runs per day, counted in UTC. After that the action asks until the next day. |
| Always ask first | A saved rule still applies when you have turned on **Always ask first**. |
| Person | Applies only to you: signed in in the browser, or in a run of your own task that you or its schedule started. Other people in the workspace have their own rules. |

Payments, deletions, publications, settings, new accounts and credentials can never be saved as a rule.

When an action runs because of a rule, the conversation reads “…, per your rule” with the link **Open rules**.

### Always ask first

If you want to confirm every step that writes yourself, turn on the rule **Always ask first**.

1. Open **Settings** and, in it, **Rules**.
2. Turn on **Always ask first**.

From then on SubKit asks before every step that saves, sends, creates or changes something, even when your request covers it. Reading still runs without a question. Your saved rules keep applying, and so does an approval for live runs. The setting applies only to you: in every conversation, to tools an AI client calls on your behalf over MCP, and to direct tool calls, also with your own API key. It does not apply to a system account and its keys, because no person stands behind them. Task runs started by their schedule follow their request and their standing permission.

### View and revoke rules

1. Open **Settings** and, in it, **Rules**.
2. **Active** lists your rules. Chips show connector, recipients, content, validity and today’s use, for example “until …” and “today 3/20”; below them “Last used …”. **Offered** lists rules you have not decided on yet.
3. Select **Revoke** on a rule and confirm.

After the revocation SubKit asks again before carrying out this action. Anything already sent stays sent.

When an action asks although a rule exists, the card names the reason:

| What you read | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| “Your rule for this action has expired. Renew it under Rules.” | The 90 days are over. |
| “Your rule for this action has reached its limit for today.” | The action already ran 20 times today through this rule. |
| “Your rule covers a different text than this one.” | The text differs from what the rule covers. |

### Limits of this check

The check is strict on purpose and asks when in doubt. It still is not an understanding of your request. You should know this:

- **SubKit recognizes requests by words and sentence structure.** It knows German and English phrasings. An unusual phrasing or another language leads to the question, even if you meant it that way.
- **SubKit reads the effect from the operation.** It concludes from the method, the path, the field names and the connector template whether something is a payment, a deletion or a publication. If an operation has a harmless name at the service and still triggers something like that, SubKit does not notice.
- **SubKit checks what it sends, not what the service does with it.** If a service forwards a message to a list, SubKit only sees the address of the list.
- **A few added words can change the tone.** The content stays yours, but the greeting, the closing and up to three words come from SubKit.
- **A rule with changing text checks the origin, not the meaning.** It covers any text you wrote or saw as a draft, to the recipients named.
- **Renewing is not possible on the Rules page yet.** The page shows neither the expiry date nor the daily limit and offers no renewal. An expired rule asks every time, and SubKit does not offer it again. It can only be renewed through the route `POST /v1/approval-rules/{id}/renew` from a browser session.
- **The daily limit and the duration are fixed.** You cannot set them.

### If something does not work

| What you see | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| “You chose to have SubKit ask before every step that writes.” | **Always ask first** is on. Select **Allow once**, or turn the rule off under **Settings › Rules**. |
| “You did not ask for this action in your own words.” | Write the request as a sentence of its own, for example “Send the summary to anna@example.com”. |
| “The request stands in pasted or quoted text, not in your own words.” | Write the request above or before the pasted text. |
| “Your request came with a condition or a ‘not’, so SubKit asks.” | Check the card and select **Allow once**, or phrase it without a condition. |
| “You did not name this recipient.” or “You did not name this target.” | Name the address or the target in your message. |
| “The action contains a value you did not state.” | Check the value on the card. State it yourself next time. |
| “The text is not yours and you have not seen it as a draft yet. Read it before it goes out.” | Read the **Content** on the card. Or ask for a draft first and then ask for it to be sent. |
| “SubKit does not know what this operation does, so it asks.” | This operation always asks. Check the card and decide. |
| “You asked for this once, and that already ran. A repeat asks again.” | If it should run once more, select **Allow once**. |
| “You did not ask for this action in your own words.” after a while | The job of your request is over: you wrote a new message, or 2 hours passed, or the task run reached its deadline. Ask again, or select **Allow once**. |
| “Only you, signed in in the browser, can let an action run without this question.” | You work with an API key or from another client. Open the conversation in the Cockpit. |
| “The rule was not saved. Nothing changed; SubKit keeps asking.” | Select **Save as rule** again. If it stays that way, check that you are signed in in the browser. |

### The same over the HTTP API

Rules belong to a person. A system account has none, and the routes answer it with `403 person_required`. You set **Always ask first** with `PUT /v1/identity/me/setup` and the field `ask_before_writing`.

| Route | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /v1/approval-rules` | Lists your offered and active rules. `?state=` filters by `offered`, `active`, `dismissed` or `revoked`. |
| `POST /v1/approval-rules/{id}/accept` | Stores an offered rule. Works only from a browser session. |
| `POST /v1/approval-rules/{id}/dismiss` | Declines an offered rule. It is not offered again. |
| `POST /v1/approval-rules/{id}/renew` | Renews an active rule for 90 days from now, also when it has already expired. Works only from a browser session. |
| `DELETE /v1/approval-rules/{id}` | Revokes an active rule. |

When the state of the rule does not fit the route, the engine answers `409 approval_rule_wrong_state`. Every field of a rule is listed in “Reference: desktop app, rules, schedules and problem reports”.
## Find your way in the Cockpit

This chapter is for anyone who works in the Cockpit every day.
Afterwards you can show and hide the navigation and the side panel with the keyboard, read an error notice and tell whether something runs in test or in production.

### The two panels

The Cockpit has the navigation on the left and the side panel on the right. The page you work on sits between them.

| Panel | Content | Shortcut |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Navigation, left | The areas of the Cockpit, for example **Chat**, **Inbox** and **Workflows**. | ⌘B, on Windows and Linux Ctrl+B |
| **Side panel**, right | **Chat**, **Details** and **History** for what you are looking at. | ⌘J, on Windows and Linux Ctrl+J |

1. Press ⌘B to shrink the navigation to a narrow icon rail. Press it again to open it.
2. Press ⌘J or select **Open side panel** in the page header.
3. Drag the edge of the side panel to change its width. With the keyboard, use the arrow keys once the edge has the focus.
4. Press Esc inside the side panel to close it.

The Cockpit remembers in this browser whether the side panel is open, how wide it is and which tab was selected. In a narrow window the side panel lies over the page instead of standing next to it.

### The three tabs of the side panel

| Tab | What it shows |
| --- | --- |
| **Chat** | A conversation next to the page. On an opened page it reads “The chat knows what you are looking at here.”, otherwise “Ask about anything in this workspace.” The chat pages themselves do not have this tab. |
| **Details** | The sections **Status** and **Technical** for what you opened: IDs, versions, times and environment. |
| **History** | The audit log entries for this one object. **Show everything in the audit log** opens the whole list. |

Good to know:

- Technical details live on the **Details** tab and no longer on the page. The page stays with what you have to decide.
- When you open a run next to a page, **Details** shows the status and the facts of that run.
- **History** needs `audit:read`. Without the permission you read “Your role does not include the audit log.”
- When nothing is open, it reads “No details here”. Open a workflow, a task or a connector.

### Read an error notice

When something goes wrong, the notice appears where it happened: in the card, in the dialog or above the list. Every notice has the same structure.

| Part | What it says |
| --- | --- |
| Title | What happened. |
| Text | What that means for you. When it has nothing of its own, you read “Nothing was changed.” |
| One button | The one action that helps, for example **Try again**, **Sign in again**, **Review approval**, **Fix it in the chat** or **Ask an administrator**. |
| **Technical details** | Collapsed. It holds **Code**, **HTTP status**, **Request ID** and **Time**. |

1. Read the title and the text.
2. Select the action offered.
3. If it does not help, expand **Technical details** and select **Copy details** or **Report a bug**.

When a list or a page cannot be loaded, it offers **Try again**. “Report a bug” describes how to report a problem.

### Tell test from production

SubKit separates two environments: **Test** and **Production**. A label with one of these two words appears wherever the environment decides about the effect:

- on the items under **Needs you** on the **Overview**,
- on the connectors of a workflow and in the connector catalog,
- in the approval dialog and on the notice about an approval that ends,
- in the technical details of a task.

Read the label before you approve or renew something. An approval only ever applies to the environment named.

### View Markdown documents

Skills, knowledge sources, items in the **Inbox** and files that contain Markdown open in the same document view.

1. Open the document.
2. Under **View**, choose between **Rendered** and **Markdown**. **Rendered** shows the formatted text, **Markdown** the source for reading and copying.
3. In longer documents, jump to a heading through **Contents**. The table of contents appears from three headings on when the column is wide enough.

### If something does not work

| What you see | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| ⌘J does not open the side panel | On Windows and Linux, use Ctrl+J, without Shift and Alt. Otherwise select **Open side panel** in the page header. |
| The hint on the button names only ⌘J | The hint always shows the Mac shortcut. On Windows and Linux, Ctrl+J works. |
| “The history could not be loaded. Nothing was changed.” | Open the tab again. If it stays that way, select **Show everything in the audit log**. |
| The **Chat** tab is missing | You are on a chat page. There the conversation already is the page. |
| “This could not be loaded” | Select **Try again**. |
## Notifications and quiet hours

This chapter is for anyone who wants to hear from SubKit when something waits for them, but not at any hour.
Afterwards you can switch on notifications on a device, limit them to your working hours or to one delivery a day, and route approval notifications to another person.

### What notifies you

SubKit only reports what a person is needed for: something was stopped, something is failing or a decision is waiting.

| Way | What you get | Delayed by quiet hours |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The **Needs you** list on the **Overview** | Every open item with cause and action. | Never. The list is always current. |
| Push in the browser or in the installed web app | One notification per item. A click opens the item. | Yes, according to your choice in **Setup**. |
| SubKit Desktop | A notification of the operating system and the number on the icon. | According to the quiet hours you set in the app. |
| Subscriptions, webhooks and the `subkit` inbox | Events for programs and for the terminal. | Never. |

A notification says what happened and what to do. Names of workflows or connectors, content and approval buttons never appear in a browser push.

### Switch on notifications on a device

1. Open **Settings** and, in it, **Your profile**.
2. Under “Do you want notifications on this device?”, switch on **Notify on this device**.
3. Allow the notifications in your browser’s dialog.

The setting applies to this browser only. Repeat it on every device where you want notifications.
Above it, “Is SubKit installed on this device?” shows whether the app is installed and whether notifications are on. “Cockpit as an app” describes how to install.

### Decide when SubKit notifies you

1. Open **Settings** and, in it, **Setup**.
2. Select **Change** on **Notifications**.
3. Answer “When may SubKit notify you?” and select **Apply**.

| Choice | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| **Right away** | Push arrives as soon as an item is new or changes. This is the default. |
| **Only during my working hours** | You enter **From** and **Until**, preset to 08:00 and 18:00. Below that you choose your **Working days**; Monday to Friday are preset, and at least one day has to be chosen. Outside this time and on the other days SubKit holds push back until the next start. A period across midnight is possible and belongs to the day it starts on. |
| **Once a day as a summary** | You enter **At**, preset to 08:00. SubKit delivers at most once a day, as soon as this time is reached. |

What happens while push is held back:

- Nothing that is still open gets lost. At the next delivery SubKit reports every new item that is still open then.
- SubKit no longer reports what was settled in the meantime.
- At the daily time and at the start of your working hours, more than one new item arrives as a single summary, such as “5 items need you” with “2 failing, 3 decisions”. It opens the newest item. A single new item arrives as the usual notification.
- If nothing new is open at the daily time, no message is sent.
- The **Needs you** list shows everything at once, whatever you choose here.

You can change the same choice under **Settings › Notifications** too. **Quiet hours** with **From** and **Until** holds push back outside your working hours: **From** is the end of your working hours, **Until** their start. **Daily summary** with its time switches on the summary. Under **More options** you find **Notify on** for your working days, **Critical items may break through quiet hours** and **Time zone**, as soon as quiet hours or the daily summary are on.

### Which time zone applies

The times apply in the time zone of the workspace. It is set under **Settings › Workspace** at “Which time zone do you work in?”. Scheduled runs follow the same time zone.

If you work in a different time zone than your team, you can store your own: in **Setup** in the question on **Notifications** at **Time zone**, or under **Settings › Notifications › More options** at **Time zone**. The field appears as soon as you choose working hours or the daily summary. Over the HTTP API it is the field `timezone`, see below.

### Pause notifications

Pause notifications for a while, for example during a meeting, without changing your schedule.

1. In SubKit Desktop, open the menu bar icon and select **Pause notifications for 1 hour**. In the Cockpit, open **Settings › Notifications**.
2. To end the pause early, select **Resume notifications**.

During the pause, SubKit sends no push notifications and shows no desktop banners. The **Needs you** list and its count keep updating. Urgent items still reach you if you switched them on. The pause applies on all your devices at once: the desktop app, the Cockpit and the installed web app read the same state. A pause lasts at most 30 days.

### Get urgent items despite quiet hours

Two kinds of items count as critical:

- A workflow in production was stopped.
- A stored secret can no longer be read.

By default these items wait for your next delivery too. With the setting `critical_breakthrough` they arrive at once, also outside working hours and before the daily delivery. In the Cockpit you switch it on in the same question or under **Settings › Notifications › More options** with **Critical items may break through quiet hours**; the HTTP API works too, see below.

### Route approval notifications to another person

If another person on your team approves what SubKit may do, route the notifications about it to them.

1. Open **Settings › Setup** and select **Change** on **Approvals**.
2. Answer “Who approves what SubKit may do?” with **Someone else on the team** and enter the **Email address**.
3. Select **Apply**. The row **Approvals** then shows the person.

What applies then:

- It affects the items that need an approval: a version waits for approval, a schedule waits for an approval, an approval or a standing permission ends soon or is missing.
- These items no longer trigger a push for you. The other person gets it when they are an active member of the workspace and may give the approval themselves. If they may not, the push stays with you.
- A prepared invitation carries the role **Member**. This role may approve.
- The items stay in your **Needs you** list, with “Waiting for approval from …”. If the person may not give the approval, that line is missing and the item stays your decision.
- If the person is not in the workspace yet, everything stays with you until they have joined.

What you read below the choice:

| What you read | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| “… is in this workspace.” | The notifications go to this person. |
| “An invitation for … is prepared and not accepted yet.” | The notifications stay with you until the person accepts the invitation. |
| “… is not in this workspace yet. An administrator has to invite this address first.” | Ask an administrator for the invitation, or select **Open People** if you are one. As soon as the address is invited, your choice applies by itself; you do not have to make it again. |
| “… cannot approve with the current role. Approval notifications stay with you until an administrator changes the role.” | Ask an administrator to give the person the role **Member** or **Administrator**, or name someone else. |
| “Invitation prepared” | You are an administrator and named an unknown address. SubKit prepared an invitation and sent no email. Pass on the **Invitation link** yourself. It is shown only once. |

### Decide from Slack

When a notification rule posts to a Slack channel, items that need a decision arrive as a card.

| Item | Buttons in Slack |
| --- | --- |
| A task run waits for your approval | **Approve**, **Decline**, **Open in SubKit** |
| The result of a task run waits for you to confirm it | **Open in SubKit** |
| The approval of a workflow expires soon | **Open in SubKit** |

Confirming a result and approving a workflow need a signed-in session in the Cockpit, so these cards link there.

What happens when you select **Approve** or **Decline**:

1. SubKit checks that the click comes from Slack: the signature made with the app’s signing secret and a timestamp no older than five minutes. A click that arrives twice counts once.
2. SubKit looks up the person your Slack account is linked to. If it is not linked yet, only you see a message with **Link Slack account** and **Open in SubKit**. To link it, select **Link Slack account**, sign in, check the Slack account shown and select **Link account**. You do this once.
3. SubKit checks at the moment of the click whether this person may decide: an active member with the permission `conversation:approve` or `workflow:write`, and for a task run its owner or an administrator. If not, only you see “You don’t have permission to decide this. Nothing was changed.”
4. SubKit records the decision in the audit log with the source `slack`, the Slack user ID and the SubKit person.
5. The message changes for everyone in the channel: it names the outcome, who decided and when. A later click shows the state, for example “Already approved.” or “The deadline has passed. Nothing was changed.”

**Open in SubKit** always works, with or without a linked account.

#### Set up the Slack app

The Slack app of your chat workspace needs these settings:

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| **Interactivity & Shortcuts › Request URL** | `https://<your SubKit address>/v1/chat/slack/interactions`, the same URL that already serves questions in chat |
| **OAuth & Permissions › Bot token scopes** | `chat:write` to post and update cards; `chat:write.public` if SubKit posts to channels the app was not added to |
| **Basic Information › Signing Secret** | the value of `platform.slack.signing_secret` in SubKit |

SubKit builds the links from `server.public_base_url`. Without it, the cards carry no **Open in SubKit** and no **Link Slack account** button. An administrator can also link accounts with `POST /v1/chat/identities`.

### Limits

- **The choice applies to push, not to the desktop app.** SubKit Desktop reads the list directly and follows the quiet hours you set in the app. More in “SubKit Desktop”.
- **The summary only names the count per kind.** The **Needs you** list shows which items they are.
- **A person without the right to approve gets no notifications.** If the person named is an active member but may not give the approval, the push stays with you, and **Settings** › **Setup** warns you. Your **Needs you** list then does not name the person, and the item stays your decision. Name a person who may approve.
- **The Cockpit does not show whom an item waits for.** The API returns the field `waiting_on` for it.
- **Messages already sent cannot be taken back.** When you switch to working hours, it applies from the next check on.

### If something does not work

| What you see | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| “Browser permission was denied. Allow notifications in your browser settings.” | Allow notifications for the Cockpit address in your browser settings. |
| No push arrives although something is open | Check **Quiet hours** and **Daily summary** under **Settings › Notifications**. Outside working hours and before the daily time, SubKit holds push back. |
| Push arrives at the wrong hour | Check the time zone of the workspace under **Settings › Workspace**. |
| “Enter a time such as 08:00.” | Write the time with four digits and a colon. |
| “The setting was not applied” | Nothing was changed. Your earlier choice still applies. Try again. |
| The other person gets no approval notifications | Check that they are a member, have push switched on on their device and may approve. |

### The same over the HTTP API

`GET /v1/identity/me/setup` reads your choice, `PUT /v1/identity/me/setup` changes it. Fields you leave out keep their value.

```bash
curl -s -X PUT "$SUBKIT_URL/v1/identity/me/setup" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SUBKIT_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"notifications":{"mode":"working_hours","from":"08:00","to":"18:00","days":[1,2,3,4,5]},"timezone":"Europe/Berlin","critical_breakthrough":true}'
```

Every field is listed in “Reference: desktop app, rules, schedules and problem reports”.
## Keep an eye on schedules

This chapter is for anyone whose workflows or tasks run on a schedule.
Afterwards you can read why a run failed, why a schedule waits or was paused, and what became of each scheduled time.
You also know how to resume a schedule and how to renew an approval before it ends.

### What you need

- A workflow or a task with a schedule. “Your first workflow” and “Hand over a goal as a task” describe how to create one.
- To read the history: `execution:read` for workflows, `task:read` for tasks.
- To resume a schedule: `workflow:write`.

### Read why a run failed

A failed run shows a notice with three parts: what happened, one recommended action and the collapsed **Technical details**.

1. Open the run through **Runs** or through the **Needs you** list on the **Overview**.
2. Read the cause and select the recommended action.

| Cause | Recommended action |
| --- | --- |
| **Sign-in rejected** | **Sign in again**: reconnect the connector. |
| **Approval no longer matches**, **Refused before the start** | **Review approval**: check and renew the approval. |
| **Timed out**, **Aborted**, **Connector unavailable**, **Provider rate limit reached**, **Not read completely**, **Error in the external system** | **Try again** |
| **AI budget reached** | **Ask an administrator**: an administrator raises the budget under **Settings** › **Budget** or continues this month without a limit. |
| **Connector missing**, **Unresolved placeholder**, **Answer in an unexpected shape**, **Message malformed**, **Not classified** | **Fix it in the chat**: the chat opens with the question about cause and fix. |

For confidential workflows (`execution_privacy: sensitive`) SubKit stores no failure details. From this version on, such a run still keeps its cause and one fixed sentence that says what to do. Example: “The connected service rejected the sign-in. Reconnect the connector, then run again. Nothing was changed by this step.” When SubKit recognizes no cause, it stays at “Sensitive execution failed.” The engine writes these sentences in English. The Cockpit says them in your language where it knows the cause, the reason for a hold or the failure code: on the overview for held and failing workflows, for a refused rerun and in error notices. In the technical details of a run, over the HTTP API and in `subkit` the engine’s English sentence remains. SubKit Desktop notifies in your language too.

### See what a schedule will cost

Before you create or change a schedule, and on every schedule, SubKit shows an estimate like “≈ €4.20 / month” with its basis, for example “from 12 runs, current model prices”.

- SubKit takes the average model cost of the last finished runs of the current version and multiplies it by the runs a month the rhythm makes.
- If the current version has not finished a run yet, SubKit takes the runs of earlier versions and says so.
- Without any finished run you read “No estimate yet”.
- Prices are the current model rates, in the currency set under **Usage**. Other costs, for example of external services, are not included.

The estimate follows the rhythm while you change it. You also see it on a schedule that waits for approval on the **Overview**.

### Why a schedule waits

A held schedule starts no run but loses nothing. As soon as you fix the reason, it goes on. The reason is shown on the workflow, on the **Overview** and in the **Schedule history**.

| What you read | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| “Held: this version has no approval. Approve it and the schedule runs again.” | Open the workflow, review it and give the approval. |
| “Held: the approval no longer applies. Renew it and the schedule runs again.” | The approval has expired, is used up or was revoked. Renew it. |
| “Held: the run is missing input. Add it in the schedule.” | Enter the missing input in the schedule. |
| “Held: the task has no standing permission. Give it and the schedule runs again.” | Open the task and select **Allow**. |
| “Held: the standing permission has ended. Renew it and the schedule runs again.” | Open the task and select **Allow**. |

### What happens after repeated failures

When a scheduled workflow run fails several times in a row for the same reason, SubKit slows the schedule down and then pauses it.

| Failures in a row | What SubKit does |
| --- | --- |
| 1 and 2 | Nothing. The next scheduled time runs as planned. |
| 3 | Waits 2 minutes after the last failure before the next run starts. |
| 4 | Waits 6 minutes after the last failure. |
| 5 | Pauses the schedule. No run starts until you resume it. |

- A failure is a scheduled run that failed or timed out. A run started by hand does not count.
- A successful run, a stopped run or a failure with a different cause ends the streak.
- Scheduled times that fall into a waiting period appear in the history as “Skipped: after repeated failures the schedule waits longer before it tries again.”
- SubKit reports the pause exactly once: as the item “Paused after repeated failures” under **Needs you**, as a push notification and as the event `schedule.auto_paused`.
- This applies to schedules of workflows. Schedules of tasks are not slowed down and not paused automatically.

### Resume a paused schedule

1. Open the workflow. At the top you read “Schedule paused automatically” with the number of failures and the date since which no run has started.
2. Fix the cause. If it is the approval, the notice offers **Renew approval**. Renew the approval first.
3. Select **Resume schedule**. You read “Schedule resumed”.

After resuming, SubKit counts failures afresh. The pause changed nothing else: workflow, approval and schedule are as they were.

### Read the schedule history

The history shows what became of each scheduled time.

1. Open the workflow or the task and select the **Schedule** tab.
2. Under **Schedule history**, read the entries, newest first. **Show older** loads more.
3. Select **Open the run** on an entry to see the run that belongs to it.

| Entry | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| “On time” | The run started at the scheduled time. |
| “Started later than planned, because the engine was busy or not running.” | The run started more than 5 minutes after the scheduled time. |
| “Ran once for several missed times instead of catching up on each.” | Several missed times became one run. |
| “Skipped: this schedule does not run on weekends.” | The schedule excludes weekends. |
| “Skipped: this day is excluded in the schedule.” | The day is among the exceptions of the schedule. |
| “Skipped: the previous run was still going.” | A task only ever has one open run. |
| “Not started: the schedule paused itself after the same failure repeated.” | Resume the schedule as described above. |
| “Held: …” | The schedule waits for you. The reasons are in “Why a schedule waits”. |

Good to know:

- When the same reason repeats, SubKit merges the scheduled times into one entry. “Stands for 12 scheduled times” names the number.
- The history goes back 90 days. SubKit deletes older entries.
- A schedule that runs more often than once a minute writes no entry for runs on time.

### Renew an approval before it ends

A workflow approval and the standing permission of a task can have an end date. SubKit announces the end in two stages: a notice in the overview 7 days before, with push also on your devices, and a notification through channels and rules 3 days before.

| When | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| 7 days before: notice | A notice such as “The approval ends in 5 days” with **Renew** appears on the workflow or the task. An item appears under **Needs you**, and with push switched on the notice also reaches your devices. |
| 3 days before: notification | SubKit sends the event `workflow.approval_expiring` or `task.grant_expiring` once to subscriptions, webhooks and the `subkit` inbox. |
| Fewer than a tenth of the runs left | For an approval with a run limit, the item under **Needs you** appears as well. |

1. Select **Renew** in the notice or on the item under **Needs you**.
2. For a workflow the approval dialog opens, for a task the standing-permission dialog. Check what it lists and choose the new validity.
3. Confirm.

**Renew** extends nothing by itself. Only your confirmation in the dialog gives the new approval.

The event is sent only when the end would change something: the workflow has an active schedule in this environment or, in production, an active inbound webhook, and no longer-running approval covers the same version. For a task, a schedule or a one-time start that has not happened yet must be pending.

### Stop a running run

1. Open the running run.
2. Select **Stop this run** and confirm with **Stop run**.

The run ends right away. The schedule stays active. Steps that already reached an external system may have been carried out.

### Limits

- **The thresholds are fixed.** The waiting periods, the pause after five failures, the 90 days of history and the announcement periods cannot be set.
- **Missing input pauses nothing.** A schedule that lacks input is held and shows up on the **Overview**, but does not count as a failure.
- **The cause of the pause is coarse for confidential workflows.** For them SubKit counts all failures without a recognized cause as the same cause.
- **Some reasons for tasks have no text of their own.** When the standing permission is used up, no longer fits the changed task, the owner is missing, the AI provider is missing or the task is paused, the history only reads “Held until you act.” The task page shows the exact reason.
- **The `subkit` inbox of existing workspaces does not get the new events by itself.** Add them to the stored rule with `subkit notifications rules`.

### If something does not work

| What you see | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| “The schedule could not be resumed and stays paused.” | Check that you have `workflow:write` and try again. |
| The schedule pauses again shortly after resuming | The cause still exists. Open the latest run, read the cause and fix it first. |
| “The schedule history could not be loaded” | Select **Try again**. |
| “No scheduled time has come up yet.” | The schedule is new or paused. Entries appear only once a scheduled time was due. |
| The **Schedule** tab is missing on the workflow | You lack `execution:read`. Ask an administrator for it. |
| In the German Cockpit a notice names the cause in English, marked “Wortlaut der Engine” | The Cockpit does not know this code yet and therefore shows the engine’s sentence. The action next to it is translated. |

### The same in the terminal and over the HTTP API

With the `subkit` command line:

```bash
subkit schedules list
subkit schedules pause <schedule-id>
subkit schedules resume <schedule-id>
```

`subkit schedules resume` also resumes an automatically paused schedule and counts failures afresh. `subkit schedules list` shows the monthly estimate in the column `estimate`. There is no `subkit` command for the history.

| Route | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /v1/workflows/{id}/schedule-occurrences` | Reads the history of a workflow, newest first. Needs `workflow:read`. |
| `GET /v1/tasks/{id}/schedule-occurrences` | Reads the history of a task. Needs `task:read`, and you must be allowed to see the task. |
| `PUT /v1/schedules/{id}` with `{"paused": false}` | Resumes a schedule. Needs `workflow:write`. |
| `GET /v1/schedules` | Lists schedules, each with `cost_projection`. Needs `workflow:read`. |
| `GET /v1/workflows/{id}/schedule-cost?cron=…&timezone=…` | Estimates the monthly cost for a rhythm before you save it. Needs `workflow:read`. |
| `POST /v1/executions/{id}/cancel` | Stops a running run. |

The response fields, the events and the reasons are listed in “Reference: desktop app, rules, schedules and problem reports”.
## SubKit Desktop

This chapter is for anyone who wants SubKit on their Mac: to keep an eye on it all day, and to let it work with files, websites and apps on that Mac.
Afterwards you have installed SubKit Desktop, signed in, allowed what SubKit may use on your Mac, and you know how to follow and stop it in the live view.
You can also run a workspace only on your Mac and move it to a server later.

### What SubKit Desktop is

SubKit Desktop is your server’s Cockpit as a Mac app, plus three things a browser tab cannot do:

- **It stays with you.** An icon in the menu bar shows what needs you, notifications arrive while the window is closed, and the app starts when you log in.
- **It works on your Mac, if you allow it.** Chat, tasks and workflows can read and write files in folders you allowed, work in websites you allowed and use apps you allowed. Nothing of this is on until you turn it on.
- **It can run a workspace of its own.** With **Only on this Mac**, the database and the engine run on your Mac, without a server.

| SubKit Desktop does | SubKit Desktop does not |
| --- | --- |
| Show your server’s Cockpit, with the same permissions as in the browser. | Touch a folder, website or app you have not allowed. |
| Report what needs you, also when the window is closed. | Store your password. The sign-in is a session as in the browser. |
| Ask before a step on your Mac writes, unless your request covers it. | Follow instructions that a web page or a file contains. |
| Show every step on your Mac in the live view, with a Stop button. | Keep working after you stop it. Later steps don’t run. |

The table in “Cockpit as an app” shows how it differs from the installed web app.

### What you need

- A Mac with Apple Silicon and macOS 13 or later. Intel Macs and Linux are not supported. The Windows app is coming soon.
- For a server: a SubKit server of version 12.1.0 or later. Its address has to be reachable over `https://`; only `localhost` may use `http://`.
- An account you can sign in to the Cockpit with in the browser, an invitation link from your invitation email, or a new account for a workspace of your own.
- For a workspace only on your Mac: no server, but an API key of Anthropic, OpenAI or Google Gemini, or a model server on your Mac.

### Install

SubKit Desktop is a signed DMG file for Macs with Apple Silicon.

1. Download [SubKit for Mac](https://github.com/MikeBild/subkit/releases/latest/download/subkit-desktop-mac-arm64.dmg).
2. Open the DMG file.
3. Drag **SubKit** into **Applications**.
4. Start SubKit from **Applications**. On the first start, macOS asks whether you want to open an app from the internet. Select **Open**.
5. Select **Get started** and connect to SubKit Cloud at `https://subkit-cloud.mikebild.dev` or to your own server, as described in “Connect to a server”.
6. Sign in in your browser. Then allow the folders and apps SubKit may use, as described in “Let SubKit work on your Mac”.

The app updates itself, so you download it only once.

The Windows app is coming soon.

### Welcome and invitation link

On the first start you see “Welcome to SubKit Desktop”. It names four things: see what needs your approval, chat and draft workflows, get tasks done step by step, and “You stay in control”.

- **Get started** leads to “Connect server”.
- **Create a new workspace** also leads to “Connect server”. When you sign in in the browser, SubKit then asks for your name, the name of the workspace, the time zone and the key of your AI provider. After that you sign the device in as usual. This works with an account that does not belong to a workspace yet, and only when the server allows new workspaces. Otherwise the browser tells you.
- **Use an invitation link** is for an invitation email. Paste the whole link under **Invitation link** and select **Open invitation**. You read, for example, “Anna invited you to the workspace ‘Brennwerk’.” with the address and the validity. **Join and sign in** opens the invitation in your browser, and the app waits for the confirmation. Join in the browser. Right after that, the browser shows “Sign in to SubKit Desktop” (see “Sign in in the browser”, from step 3). After **Sign in** you are signed in to the app, without a second step in the app.

An invitation that has expired, was withdrawn or was already used says so. Ask the person who invited you for a new one.

### Connect to a server

1. In “Connect server”, keep **Connect to a server**. **Only on this Mac** starts a local workspace instead (see “A workspace only on this Mac”).
2. Enter the address of your server under **Server address** and select **Check connection**. **Examples** lists the servers the app already knows and `localhost:3000`.
3. Read the result. With “Connected” everything fits, and **Next** leads to the sign-in.

The app checks whether a SubKit server answers at the address and whether the versions fit together. When the server is too old, **Ask an administrator** copies a message for the person who runs it.

### Sign in in the browser

The sign-in happens in your browser, not in the app. That way you use the sign-in you already know, and the app never sees your password.

1. In the step “Sign in with browser”, select **Open browser**. Your browser opens, and the app shows “Waiting for confirmation in the browser…”.
2. Sign in to the Cockpit in the browser if you are not signed in there yet.
3. Read the page “Sign in to SubKit Desktop”. It names your Mac, the workspace and the account, for example “SubKit Desktop on MacBook-Anna is asking to sign in to Brennwerk.” and “Signed in as anna@example.com”.
4. Select **Sign in**. Continue only if you just started this sign-in yourself in the app on this device.
5. The browser hands back to the app. You read “Device registered” with the device name, the server and the status. **Open SubKit** opens the Cockpit.

With **Cancel** on the page in the browser or **Cancel** in the app, nothing happens: no profile and no device is created.
The page in the browser is valid for 10 minutes. After that, start the sign-in again in the app.

### The first start after the sign-in

The app asks up to three questions once:

1. **Workspace.** If you have access to several workspaces, choose one. You can switch later at any time.
2. **Allow notifications.** **Allow** lets macOS show SubKit’s notifications. A test notification confirms it: “Notifications are on”.
3. **Diagnostics.** “Should your bug reports include diagnostics?” **Attach diagnostics** adds a cleaned diagnostics report to every bug report you send. Diagnostics stay off unless you choose this.

**Not now** skips a question. You change all three later under **Settings** in the Cockpit.

### Menu bar, notifications and quiet hours

When you close the window, SubKit Desktop keeps running. The icon in the menu bar shows the number of open items.

| Entry in the icon’s menu | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Open SubKit** | Brings the window to the front. |
| **Needs you (3)** | Opens the list of open items. When nothing is open, it reads “Nothing needs you right now”. |
| **Open live view** | Shows what SubKit does on your Mac right now. Appears while SubKit works on your Mac. |
| **Pause notifications for 1 hour** | Holds notifications back for an hour. Below it you read until when, for example “Paused until 15:05”. **Resume notifications** ends the pause. |
| **Launch at login** | Starts SubKit Desktop with your Mac, without opening a window. |
| **Check for updates** | Looks for a new version of the app. |
| **Quick note …** | Opens a note for your inbox (⌥ Space). |
| **Settings…** | Opens the app’s settings. |
| **Report a problem…** | Opens the dialog from “Report a bug”. |
| **Quit SubKit** | Quits the app. No notifications arrive after that. |

A notification says what happened and what to do, for example “‘Daily report’ is waiting for your decision” and “Review the change and decide.” A click opens exactly this item in the window.

- A new item is reported within about a second, after a minute at the latest.
- When several items arrive at once, the app shows at most three notifications. You see the rest in the number on the icon.
- What is already open when the app starts is not reported again.

You set quiet hours in the app:

1. Open **Settings…** in the app menu or press ⌘,.
2. Switch on **Quiet hours** and enter **From** and **To**. The presets are 22:00 and 07:00.
3. If you like, switch on **Launch when you log in to your computer** and choose German, English or **Same as system** under **Language**.

During quiet hours and during a pause SubKit keeps counting but shows no notifications. The menu then reads, for example, “Quiet hours until 07:00”. Quiet hours follow the clock of your Mac.

### Quick note

Press ⌥ Space anywhere, or select **Quick note …** in the menu bar. A small window asks “What do you want to capture?”.

1. Type your note.
2. Press ⌘ ↩ or select **Into the inbox**. Esc closes the window without sending.

You read “Note in the inbox”. The note waits there for your review, as described in “Collect ideas and turn them into knowledge or skills”.

### Drop files: “Where should this go?”

Drag files onto the window, the Dock icon or the menu bar icon. SubKit asks “Where should this go?” and offers four choices:

| Choice | What happens | Limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Store as file** | The file lands under **Files**, with an `@attachment:` reference. | 5 MB per file |
| **Ingest as source** | SubKit splits it into sections and keeps it as a knowledge source. | 50 MB per file |
| **Attach in chat** | The files wait for your next chat message. | 10 files |
| **Into the inbox** | SubKit reviews it and suggests what it becomes. | 1 MB for text files |

You can drop up to 20 files at once. A choice that does not fit says why, for example “Larger than 5 MB” or “File type not supported”. While the app is offline, nothing is placed.

### Let SubKit work on your Mac

SubKit can do three things on your Mac. All three are off until you turn them on, and each uses only what you allow.

| Capability | What SubKit does | What you allow |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Files** | Reads files, saves, creates folders, moves files and puts them in the Trash. | Folders, each with **Read** or **Read and write** |
| **Browser** | Opens pages, reads them, fills in fields, presses buttons and downloads files, in a browser of its own. | Websites, as an origin such as `https://shop.example.com` |
| **Apps** | Reads and uses buttons and fields in an app window, types and takes redacted screenshots. | Apps, chosen one by one |

Turn them on:

1. Open **Settings…** in the app and, in it, **Local capabilities**. Select **Manage**.
2. Switch on **Let chat and tasks use this Mac**.
3. Under **Local allowances**, add what SubKit may use:
   - **Folders**: **Choose folder…**, then choose **Read** or **Read and write** under **Access**.
   - **Websites**: enter an origin, for example `https://shop.example.com:8443` or an address in your local network, without a path, and select **Add**.
   - **Apps**: **Choose app…**.
4. Under **Off limits for SubKit**, add what SubKit must never use.

Some things are always blocked and cannot be allowed: SubKit itself, security prompts and sign-in windows, password managers, crypto wallets, banking and payments, terminals and shells, scripts and automation, System Settings and installers, remote support and the Finder. SubKit also refuses a whole disk, a system or hidden folder and your entire home folder. Choose a subfolder instead.

The allowances live on your Mac. The server learns which folders, websites and apps the Mac offers, so an approval can name them. In the Cockpit, **Settings** › **Devices** › “Which devices run local steps?” lists every Mac with what it offers, for example “3 folders”.

Once you turn a capability on, SubKit creates a connector for it, for example “MacBook Pro (Anna): Files”, named in the language of the app. Chat and tasks use it from then on. How a workflow uses it with fixed steps is in “Reference: workflow steps on your device”.

**Remove** on an entry takes the allowance back. Workflows, tasks and chat can no longer use it afterwards.

### macOS permissions

For **Apps**, macOS has to allow SubKit two things. The top of **Local capabilities** shows each one with **Granted** or **Missing**. **Check permissions** shows only what is still missing.

| Permission | Why SubKit needs it |
| --- | --- |
| **Accessibility** | SubKit reads and uses buttons and fields in the apps you have allowed. |
| **Screen Recording** | SubKit takes screenshots of the app window with password fields blacked out. |

1. Select **Open System Settings** next to a missing permission. SubKit first asks macOS itself, so it shows up in the list, and then opens the settings.
2. Switch SubKit on in **Privacy & Security**.
3. Back in SubKit, select **Check again**. When macOS asks for it, select **Restart SubKit**.

Files and the browser need no extra permission. When macOS asks whether SubKit may access your Desktop, Documents or Downloads folder, it is because you allowed a folder there.

### When SubKit asks on your Mac

On your Mac, the same rule applies as everywhere: your request decides what runs without a question.

- **Reading and preparing run without a question.** Opening a page, reading a file, taking a screenshot, scrolling and selecting.
- **A step that writes runs without a question only when your request covers it.** Saving a file, pressing a button that sends, filling in a field, typing. Otherwise SubKit asks: in the chat with **Allow once** or **Decline**, in the live view with **Allow once** or **Deny**.
- **Some steps always ask.** Putting a file in the Trash, payments, publishing and sending to recipients you did not name.
- **Always ask first** makes every step that changes something ask you, also on your Mac. You turn it on under **Settings** › **Rules** in the Cockpit.
- **What a page says is not your request.** When a page contains an instruction, the live view shows “The page contains an instruction. SubKit does not follow it.”

“When SubKit asks” explains the rule in full.

When a page asks you to sign in, SubKit hands over to you. The live view reads “Your turn – sign in, then ‘Hand back to SubKit’”. Sign in yourself, then select **Hand back to SubKit**. SubKit does not act in the window while it is your turn.

A workflow step on your Mac needs its approval as every workflow step does. The approval names the Mac, the folders, websites and apps.

### Live view

While SubKit works on your Mac, a small bar at the top of the screen shows “SubKit is using ‘Safari’” with **Stop**. **Open live view** in the menu bar shows more:

- Where the work comes from: “Started by you in chat”, “From your task” or “From your schedule”.
- The **Latest redacted screenshot**. Password fields and fields marked as sensitive are blacked out on your Mac, before anything leaves it.
- **Steps**, each with its result, for example **Done**, **Waiting for you**, **Refused** or **Not run**.
- A question, when a step waits for you, with **Allow once** and **Deny**.

The status says what is going on:

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **Running** | SubKit is working. |
| **Waiting for you** | A step needs your decision. |
| **Waiting until you stop typing** | You are typing on your Mac. SubKit waits so it does not type into your text. |
| **Your turn – sign in, then “Hand back to SubKit”** | A sign-in is handed to you. |
| **Stopped. Later steps won’t run.** | You stopped it. |
| **Device unavailable** | The Mac lost its connection to the server. |
| **Finished** | Everything is done. |

**Stop** or ⌘⇧⎋ stops SubKit at once, from any app. The step that is running ends, and later steps don’t run. The run shows which steps were done.

Screenshots of a run are kept encrypted for 30 days and then deleted. In the Cockpit, the person of the device can see a run’s redacted screenshot on its steps.

### A workspace only on this Mac

With **Only on this Mac**, SubKit runs the database and the engine on your Mac, without a server. Besides your AI provider and the services your workflows call, nothing leaves the Mac. That suits trying SubKit out, or working alone.

1. In “Connect server”, select **Only on this Mac**.
2. **Data folder**: keep the suggested folder or choose **Choose another folder…**. The folder has to be on this Mac and must not be synced, for example not in iCloud Drive.
3. **You**: enter **Your name**.
4. **AI access**: choose a **Provider** (Anthropic, OpenAI or Google Gemini) and enter its **API key**, or choose **Local model server** and enter its address, for example `http://localhost:11434`. The key is stored encrypted in your local workspace. **Set up later** skips this step; workflows without AI run anyway.
5. **Setting up**: SubKit starts the database, the engine and the workspace. Then the Cockpit opens.

The local workspace runs while the app is open and the Mac is awake.

Under **Settings…** › **Local workspace** you find:

- **Running** or **Stopped**, and the size of the data.
- **Backups**: SubKit makes one automatically before every update and before every restore. **Create backup** makes one by hand. **Restore** replaces the workspace with a backup. Newer changes are lost; allowed folders stay.
- **Open at login**: starts the local workspace when you log in.
- **Move to a server**: exports the workspace as a bundle and imports it into your server workspace (see below).
- **Remove all local data**: stops the engine, moves the data to the Trash and forgets the keys. Workflows, runs and backups on this Mac are gone afterwards.

A model on a local model server has to be able to call tools. If it cannot, you read “Model can’t call tools”: chat and tasks don’t work with it, workflows keep running. Choose another model or a provider key under **Settings** › **AI assistant** in the Cockpit.

#### Move to a server

1. Under **Local workspace**, select **Move to a server**.
2. Enter the server address with `https://` and select **Move now**. SubKit exports the workspace for the server and stops it on this Mac.
3. Sign in to the server. The workspace now runs there.

This Mac stays connected as a device with its allowed folders. You renew the approvals of your workflows on the server. The local data stays on the Mac until you remove it. **Export bundle** saves the bundle without moving, for example to import it yourself.

### Devices and signing out

Every Mac on which you sign in with SubKit Desktop is a device of its own with its own session. The server lists it under the name of the Mac. When you sign in again on the same Mac, it stays the same device.

- **Sign out** in the account menu of the Cockpit ends the session of this device. Your session in the browser and other devices stay signed in.
- **Remove** in the list **Your servers** deletes the local session and the profile. Nothing changes on the server.
- **Revoking a device** signs it out from outside, for example after a loss. Within a few seconds the app then shows “Signed out of …” with **Sign in again**.

You see your devices in the Cockpit under **Settings** › **Devices**. The list shows the installed web app and every desktop device with its kind, name, the day it signed in and its last use. The device you are sitting at carries the mark **This device**.

1. Open the Cockpit in the browser and there **Settings** › **Devices**.
2. Select **Revoke** at the device.
3. Confirm. The dialog names the device and says what happens: it is signed out at once and no longer receives notifications; other devices stay signed in.

In the app itself you see the same list, but there you can only sign out **This device** with **Sign out**. You revoke another device in the browser.

When a Mac that runs local steps is revoked, local steps stop running on it, and approvals that name it can no longer run.

### How long you stay signed in

| Rule | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Without use | 30 days. Any use of the app, also in the background at the menu bar icon, starts the period again. |
| At most | 90 days since the sign-in, even with daily use. After that you sign in again in the browser. |
| After a revocation or **Sign out** | Ended at once. |

When the session expires you read “Session expired” and “Sign in again; your settings are kept.” Shorter periods apply to the browser and the installed web app: 8 hours without use, 24 hours at most.

### Several servers

If you work with several SubKit servers, each one gets its own profile with its own session.

1. In the **Servers** menu, select **Add server…** or press ⌘N.
2. Connect and sign in as above.
3. Switch between the profiles through the **Servers** menu or with **Open** in the list **Your servers**.

### Updates

The app checks for updates at start and every six hours after that. If **Settings** reads “Automatic updates are not enabled in this build.”, your build was made without updates. Download SubKit again as described in “Install”.

| What you read | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| “You’re on the latest version, ….” | Nothing to do. |
| “Version … is available. The download starts shortly.” | The app downloads the update in the background. |
| “Version … is downloaded. Restart SubKit to install it.” | Select **Restart now**. With **Later**, the update is installed the next time you quit. |
| “The update could not be verified and was not installed. …” | Your version stays as it is. Try again later. |
| “Runs still active in the local workspace: …. A restart stops them.” | Wait until the runs are done, or select **Restart anyway**. |

When the server requires a newer app, you read it while connecting. Update SubKit Desktop then.

### Limits

- **Notifications only arrive while the app runs.** After **Quit SubKit** it reports nothing. For notifications without a running app, use the push of the web app.
- **What was new during quiet hours or a pause is not reported later.** You see it in the number on the icon and in the **Needs you** list.
- **The quiet hours of the app are its own.** The choice under **Settings › Setup** in the Cockpit applies to push in the browser, not to the app.
- **The app reports the items of the opened profile.** Other servers report only once you switch to them.
- **Local steps run only while the app is open and the Mac is awake.** A run that needs the Mac waits for it and says “A run is waiting for its device to come online.”
- **Browser and app steps run only for the person of the Mac.** From their chat or task, a run they start, or a schedule they set up.
- **Redaction covers password fields and fields marked as sensitive.** A secret that a page or app shows as plain text stays in the screenshot.
- **SubKit Desktop runs only on the Mac for now.** The Windows app is coming soon.

### If something does not work

| What you see | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| “Server not reachable” | Check the address and whether you can reach the server in the browser. |
| “Not a SubKit server” | Enter the address of the server, without `/cockpit` at the end. |
| The address does not start with `https` | Use the `https` address of your server. |
| “Version … isn’t supported” | The server is too old for the app. Select **Ask an administrator** and pass the message on. |
| “App too old” | Update SubKit Desktop. |
| “Sign-in not supported” | Update the server or SubKit Desktop. |
| “This isn’t a complete invitation link.” | Copy the whole link from the invitation email. |
| “This invitation has expired” or “This invitation was already used” | Ask the person who invited you for a new invitation. |
| “Sign-in expired, start it again” | At most one minute may pass between **Sign in** in the browser and the return to the app. Start the sign-in again. |
| “The server declined” | Start again. If it stays that way, check that your account is active in the workspace. |
| “The browser couldn’t be opened” | Check that a default browser is set up on your Mac. |
| Nothing happens in the app after **Sign in** in the browser | Allow the browser to open SubKit when it asks. If the app is no longer running, start it and begin again. |
| “Server offline” | SubKit tries to restore the connection automatically. The icon shows “No connection to the server”. |
| “SubKit can’t allow this folder.” | Choose a subfolder, not a whole disk, a system or hidden folder, or your entire home folder. |
| “An allowed folder was replaced. Allow it again.” | The folder was deleted and created again. Remove it under **Local capabilities**, choose it again and renew the approvals that name it. |
| “This device is missing a system permission.” | Open **Check permissions** under **Local capabilities** and grant the missing permission. |
| A step is **Refused** | The folder, website or app is not allowed, or it is off limits. Allow it under **Local capabilities**, or ask SubKit for something else. |
| “Model can’t call tools” | Choose a model that calls tools or a provider key under **Settings** › **AI assistant**. |
| “Port is busy” | Select **Use another port**. |
| “The database can’t run here.” | Choose a folder on this Mac that isn’t synced. |
| “Local workspace doesn’t start” | Select **Try again**. If it stays that way, report a problem with diagnostics. |
| No notifications arrive | Check whether a pause or quiet hours are active and whether macOS allows notifications for SubKit. |
## Report a bug

This chapter is for anyone who notices something in the Cockpit or in SubKit Desktop.
Afterwards you can send a bug report with diagnostics and know what is sent, what is removed before and who can read the report.

### Where a report goes

A report does not leave your SubKit server. It lands as an item in the **Inbox** of your workspace, in the category `feedback`. Nobody outside gets it automatically, not even the maker of SubKit.

Every person in your workspace who may see the **Inbox** (`intake:read`) can read it. These are administrators and members, not users with the User role.

### Send a report

1. Select **Report a bug** in the page header, next to the side panel toggle. **Report a bug…** in the **User menu** and **Report a bug** in the **Technical details** of an error notice open the same dialog.
2. Under **Kind of feedback**, choose **Bug**, **Idea** or **Other**.
3. Describe what you were trying to do and what happened instead.
4. If needed, use **Attach a file** to add up to 3 files of 2 MB each: PNG, JPG, PDF, TXT or JSON.
5. Leave **Attach diagnostic report** switched on or switch it off. **View** shows exactly what goes along.
6. Check text and files for private information and select **Send feedback**.

The dialog tells you two things before you send: next to **Attach a file** it says that images and PDFs are sent as they are. Above **Send feedback** it says that the report is stored in the **Inbox** of your workspace, who reads it there, and that your text is sent as you wrote it except for secrets and file paths.

You then read “Thanks for your feedback”. When you open the dialog from an error notice, error, cause, code, request ID and time are already filled in.

When sending fails, your draft is kept: the kind, the text and the choice about the diagnostic report. You choose files and the screenshot again.

### What is sent

| Part | Content |
| --- | --- |
| What you enter | The kind of feedback and your text. |
| Files | What you attach yourself. |
| Diagnostic report, when switched on | **App** (Browser, Desktop app or Installed web app), **App version**, **Operating system**, **Server version**, **Connection status**, **Page** and the **Last 10 errors** with code and time. |
| Screenshot, only in SubKit Desktop and only when you tick it | A picture of the Cockpit window. |

Of the **Page**, only the path is sent, without parameters. Content of your workflows, runs or conversations is not sent unless you write it into the text or attach it.

### What is removed before storing

The Cockpit cleans the diagnostic report before sending, and the server cleans the whole report once more before it stores it.

| What | Where | Replaced by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Credentials in headers such as `Authorization` and `Cookie`, tokens after `Bearer`, `Basic` or `Token`, named secrets such as `password`, `api_key`, `client_secret`, and strings that look like a secret | Text, diagnostic report, text files, file names | `[removed]` |
| Parameters, fragment and user information in addresses | Text, diagnostic report, text files, file names | The address stays without these parts. |
| Absolute file paths | Text, diagnostic report, text files, file names | `[path]` |
| Email addresses | Diagnostic report, text files, file names | `[email]` |

Under “Removed before storing”, the stored item names how many places were removed.

### The screenshot in SubKit Desktop

In SubKit Desktop the dialog also offers a **Window screenshot**. The browser and the installed web app do not have it.

1. Select **Report a problem…** in the app menu, in the **Help** menu or on the icon in the menu bar. The app takes the picture before the dialog appears, so that the dialog is not in it.
2. Look at the picture in the dialog.
3. Tick **Attach this picture of the window** only when nothing confidential is visible. The box is never ticked in advance.

Password and secret fields are hidden in the picture. Anything shown openly in the window, such as a newly created API key, stays visible.

When the app is not signed in, **Report a problem…** opens the **Diagnostics** dialog instead. The data contains the app version, operating system, server version and the last 10 errors.

- If your server takes reports without sign-in, the dialog offers **Send to server**. The app then sends the diagnostics with its device ID, and you read “Thanks, your report arrived.”
- Otherwise, for example on an older server, it offers **Copy diagnostics** and **Save as file…** only. Add the data to your message to the person who runs your server.

### Write a report while offline

If SubKit cannot reach the server, write the report anyway and select **Queue**. SubKit sends it as soon as the connection is back, one report at a time, and keeps the time you wrote it. If you were signed out in the meantime, it waits until you sign in again. Each report is sent only once, even when a send is repeated. A report that could not be sent within 14 days is dropped.

### Limits

- **Email addresses in your text stay.** That is deliberate: your text is yours and is sent as you wrote it. The server removes only secrets and file paths from it. It removes email addresses from the diagnostic report, from text files and from file names.
- **Pictures and PDFs are not cleaned.** That includes the screenshot. The dialog says so next to **Attach a file**. Look at them before you send.
- **No separate readers for feedback.** The category `feedback` has the same readers as the rest of the **Inbox**: administrators and members. A report for administrators only is not provided.
- **The title of the item is English.** It starts with “Bug report:”, “Idea:” or “Feedback:”, followed by the first line of your text.
- **Two different markers.** In the German diagnostic report the Cockpit writes `[entfernt]`, the server `[removed]`, `[email]` and `[path]`.
- **Five reports in ten minutes.** After that the dialog asks you to wait a few minutes.
- **No API key.** No report can be sent with an API key or from the `subkit` command line.

### If something does not work

| What you see | What to do |
| --- | --- |
