Apache License 2.0 (`Apache-2.0`). The full text is in the `LICENSE` file of every release.


## Third-party components

Every release ships `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt` next to the binaries. It lists the license
texts of all bundled packages, the embedded embedding model and the Bun runtime.

- **Embedding model:** `paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2` by sentence-transformers,
  Apache-2.0 per the upstream Hugging Face model card; ONNX conversion by Xenova.
- **Bun runtime:** the `engine` and `subkit` executables contain the Bun runtime, which statically
  links LGPL components (JavaScriptCore/WebKit, tinycc). The section "Relinking and
  corresponding source" in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt` explains how to rebuild and relink.
- **Container image:** `/usr/local/share/subkit/` also holds `BASE_IMAGE_INVENTORY.txt`
  (operating system packages of the base image; the image contains no browser) and `SOURCE_OFFER.txt`.

The corresponding source of the GPL and LGPL components is available on request for at least
three years (written offer in the notices). Request it through the [contact form](https://subkit.mikebild.dev/kontakt). Once the SubKit repository is public, it will also
be linked there.
## Reference: desktop app, rules, schedules and problem reports

This page lists the HTTP API, the events, the audit trail and the settings for the desktop app, rules, schedules and problem reports.
It is for developers and operators who build on these parts. The task-oriented chapters are “SubKit Desktop”, “When SubKit asks”, “Keep an eye on schedules”, “Notifications and quiet hours”, “Set SubKit up for yourself” and “Report a bug”.
The complete, machine-readable description of every route is at `/openapi.json` on your engine.

### Routes

| Route | Who may call it | Does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /v1/workflows/{id}/schedule-occurrences` | `workflow:read` | Schedule history of a workflow, newest first. |
| `GET /v1/tasks/{id}/schedule-occurrences` | `task:read`, and the task must be visible to you | Schedule history of a task, newest first. |
| `GET /v1/identity/me/setup` | A person | Reads your setup choices, with recommended values where unset. |
| `PUT /v1/identity/me/setup` | A person | Stores setup choices. Fields left out keep their value. |
| `GET /v1/approval-rules` | A person | Lists your offered and active approval rules. |
| `POST /v1/approval-rules/{id}/accept` | A person in a browser session | Stores an offered rule. |
| `POST /v1/approval-rules/{id}/dismiss` | A person | Declines an offered rule. |
| `POST /v1/approval-rules/{id}/renew` | A person in a browser session | Renews an active rule for 90 days from now. |
| `DELETE /v1/approval-rules/{id}` | A person | Revokes an active rule. |
| `POST /v1/feedback` | A person in a browser session | Files a report in the workspace inbox. |
| `GET /v1/identity/desktop-login/start` | Nobody signed in; opened by the app in the browser | Starts a desktop sign-in and redirects to the confirmation page. |
| `GET` and `POST /v1/identity/desktop-login/confirm` | The person in the browser | Shows the confirmation page and takes the decision. Not part of `/openapi.json`. |
| `POST /v1/identity/desktop-session` | The desktop app, without a cookie | Exchanges the sign-in code for a Cockpit session. |
| `GET /v1/cockpit/installations` | A session of the Cockpit: browser, installed web app or desktop device | Returns `installations` with every installation of the person. `installation` names the installed web app and is filled for the session of the normal Cockpit only. |
| `POST /v1/cockpit/installations` | The session of the normal Cockpit | The answer now carries `kind`. |
| `DELETE /v1/cockpit/installations/{installationId}` | The session of the normal Cockpit for any of your installations; the session of an installation only for itself | Revokes a web app or a desktop device. |

“A person” means a user account, not a system account. A system account gets `403 person_required`. Routes that need a browser session answer other callers with `403 human_confirmation_required`.

### Schedule history

Query parameters of both routes: `limit` (default 50, at most 200) and `before` (a time in ISO 8601). The answer is `{items, next_before}`. Pass `next_before` as `before` to read older entries.

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | ID of the entry. |
| `workflow_id`, `task_id`, `schedule_id` | What the entry belongs to. |
| `due_at` | The scheduled time. |
| `last_due_at` | The last scheduled time the entry stands for, when several were merged. |
| `started_at` | When the run started, if one started. |
| `state` | `ran`, `ran_late`, `skipped` or `held`. |
| `reason_code` | Why, see the next table. Empty for a run on time. |
| `skipped_count` | How many further scheduled times the entry stands for. |
| `execution_id`, `task_run_id` | The run that belongs to the entry. |
| `run_outcome` | How that run ended: `running`, `succeeded`, `failed` or `aborted`; `null` without a run. |
| `created_at`, `updated_at` | When the entry was written and last changed. |

| `reason_code` | `state` | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `late_start` | `ran_late` | Started more than 5 minutes after the scheduled time. |
| `merged_missed` | `ran_late` | One run for several missed times. |
| `calendar_weekend` | `skipped` | The schedule excludes weekends. |
| `calendar_skip_date` | `skipped` | The day is excluded in the schedule. |
| `failure_backoff` | `skipped` | Waiting period after repeated failures. |
| `previous_run_active` | `skipped` | The previous run of the task was still open. |
| `repeated_failures` | `held` | The schedule paused itself. |
| `input_required` | `held` | The schedule lacks required input. |
| `execution_authority_required` | `held` | No approval covers the current version. |
| `execution_authority_unavailable` | `held` | The approval expired, is used up or was revoked. |
| `grant_required`, `grant_expired`, `grant_exhausted`, `grant_fingerprint_mismatch` | `held` | The standing permission of the task is missing, ended, used up or no longer fits the task. |
| `owner_unavailable`, `ai_access_missing`, `paused` | `held` | The owner of the task is unavailable, the workspace has no AI provider, or the task is paused. |

Entries are kept for 90 days. A schedule entry returned by the schedule routes now carries `auto_pause`: `null`, or `{paused_reason, failure_class, consecutive_failures, since}` while the schedule is paused after repeated failures.

A run now names the cause of a failure as `outcome.cause_class` in `GET /v1/executions/{id}` and as `failure.cause_class` in the list, also for confidential workflows. Values include `auth_failed`, `authority_mismatch`, `connector_missing`, `connector_unavailable`, `budget_exhausted`, `rate_limited`, `timeout`, `placeholder_unresolved`, `schema_mismatch`, `incomplete_read` and `payload_invalid`.

### Setup choices

| Field | Values | Sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ask_before_writing` | `true`, `false` | The rule **Always ask first**: every step that writes asks, even when the request covers it. Default `false`. |
| `default_environment` | `dev`, `prod` | The environment for new tasks and for the review of new workflows. Recommended: `dev`. |
| `approver` | `{"kind":"self"}` or `{"kind":"teammate","email":"…"}` | Who gets approval notifications. Recommended: `self`. |
| `notifications` | `{"mode":"immediately"}`, `{"mode":"working_hours","from":"HH:MM","to":"HH:MM","days":[1,2,3,4,5]}` or `{"mode":"daily_digest","at":"HH:MM"}` | When push is delivered. Recommended: `immediately`. `days` names the working days as weekdays from `1` (Monday) to `7` (Sunday), each at most once; without the field, Monday to Friday applies. |
| `timezone` | An IANA time zone, or `null` for the time zone of the workspace | The zone the times above are read in. |
| `critical_breakthrough` | `true`, `false` | Whether critical items are pushed at once despite held push. Default `false`. |
| `first_job` | Text of at most 120 characters, or `null` | The first suggestion in the Cockpit. |
| `services` | Up to 50 connector slugs | Which connectors the Cockpit offers first. |

The answer adds `unset` (which of environment, approver and notifications are not chosen yet), `recommended`, `updated_at` and, for a teammate, `approver.user_id`, `approver.invitation` with `member`, `pending` or `needs_admin`, `approver.can_approve` and `approver.missing_permissions`. `can_approve` is `true` when the person’s role holds `conversation:approve`, `task:grant` and `workflow:write`; the member role holds all three. With `false`, `missing_permissions` names the missing permissions, and approval notifications stay with the person who asks. While the person does not exist in the workspace, `can_approve` is `null`. When an administrator names an unknown address, the answer carries `invitation` with `invite_id`, `plaintext_token` and `expires_at` exactly once; the invitation carries the member role, and no email is sent. When someone without the right to invite named an address (`needs_admin`), the engine links the choice by itself as soon as an administrator invites or adds that address. `PUT` answers `409 approver_already_known` when the address already belongs to a person who cannot be invited again.

### Approval rules

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | ID of the rule. |
| `state` | `offered`, `active`, `dismissed` or `revoked`. Only `active` rules apply. |
| `tool`, `verb` | The tool and the kind of action: `send`, `create`, `update`, `run`, `save` or `other`. |
| `connector`, `account` | The connector the rule is limited to. |
| `operation`, `target` | The one operation the rule is limited to, for example `POST /v1/messages/send`. |
| `recipients` | The only recipients the rule covers. Empty: actions without a recipient. |
| `content_class` | `no_content`: only actions without text. `same_content`: only the exact text that was approved. `person_given`: only text the person wrote or saw as a draft. |
| `expires_at`, `expired` | When the rule stops applying, and whether that time has passed. |
| `daily_limit`, `uses_today` | Runs allowed per day in UTC, and runs today. |
| `approvals_count`, `use_count` | How often the person approved this action by hand, and how often the rule let it run. |
| `offered_at`, `decided_at`, `revoked_at`, `last_used_at`, `created_at` | Times. |

A route that does not fit the state of the rule answers `409 approval_rule_wrong_state`.

A tool call in a conversation carries `policy` when the chat rule looked at it: `ran_without_asking`, `rule` (`user_instruction` or `standing_rule`), `bound_action` (`verb`, `effect_class`, `target`, `account`, `recipients`, `content_summary`, `content`), `because` (`quote`, `message_id`), `rule_id`, `ask_reason`, `ask_detail` and `rule_offer`.

| `ask_reason` | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `ask_before_writing` | The person turned on **Always ask first**, so every step that writes asks. |
| `no_person` | No person stands behind the call, for example a system account or a task run someone else started. |
| `write_gate` | No current request of the person can cover the action. |
| `no_browser_session` | The caller is not a person signed in in the browser. |
| `tool_not_coverable`, `effect_class_never`, `effect_unknown` | The kind of action always asks, or its effect is unknown. |
| `no_user_message`, `no_quote`, `quote_too_short`, `quote_too_long`, `quote_not_in_user_words`, `not_a_request`, `verb_mismatch` | The person did not ask for this action in their own words. |
| `quote_in_pasted_text` | The request stands in pasted or quoted text. |
| `conditional_or_negated` | The request carries a condition or a negation. |
| `recipient_not_named`, `target_not_named`, `value_not_said`, `date_not_said`, `header_not_requested` | The action contains something the person did not state. |
| `content_not_given` | The text is not the person’s and was not shown as a draft. |
| `already_used` | The request already covered this action once. |
| `rule_expired`, `rule_daily_limit`, `rule_content` | A rule exists but does not apply. |
| `undecidable` | The check could not be completed, so the action asks. |

### Problem reports

Body of `POST /v1/feedback`:

| Field | Limits |
| --- | --- |
| `kind` | `bug`, `idea` or `other`. |
| `message` | 1 to 5,000 characters. |
| `client_request_id` | Optional UUID. Sending the same ID again does not file the report twice. |
| `diagnostics` | Optional: `app_version`, `platform`, `server_version`, `connection` (up to 200 characters each), `client_kind` (`browser`, `desktop` or `pwa`), `route` (up to 2,000 characters) and `recent_errors` (up to 10 entries with `code` and `at`). |
| `attachments` | Up to 3 entries with `filename` and `content_base64`, 2 MB each: PNG, JPG, PDF, TXT or JSON. |
| `screenshot_png_base64` | Optional PNG of at most 4 MB. |

The answer is `201` with `id`, `intake_item_id` and `replayed`. Errors: `409 report_id_taken`, `413 attachment_too_large` or `screenshot_too_large`, `422 attachment_invalid`, `attachment_type`, `attachment_rejected` or `screenshot_invalid`, and `429 rate_limit_exceeded` after 5 reports in 10 minutes per person.

### Desktop sign-in and installations

Query parameters of `GET /v1/identity/desktop-login/start`:

| Parameter | Format |
| --- | --- |
| `code_challenge` | 43 characters, base64url. |
| `code_challenge_method` | `S256`. |
| `state` | 16 to 128 characters. |
| `device_id` | A UUID the app creates once per server profile. |
| `device_label` | 1 to 64 characters without control characters. |
| `redirect_uri` | Optional: `subkit://callback` or, where accepted, `subkit-dev://callback`. |
| `app_version` | The version of the app such as `12.1.7`, also with a pre-release tag such as `12.1.7-beta.1`. Without it, or below `server.desktop_min_version`, the engine answers `426`. |

Body of `POST /v1/identity/desktop-session`: `code` (43 characters), `code_verifier` (43 to 128 characters), `app_version` and optionally `state`. The answer is `200` with `installation_id`, `cockpit_path` and `created`, and it sets the session cookie.

The start and the confirmation are pages in the browser. A browser that opens them gets every refusal below as a page with the next step and the code, never as JSON. An API client gets JSON.

| Answer | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `400 invalid_redirect_uri` | The target is not accepted by this server. |
| `401 invalid_grant` | The code is unknown, used, expired or does not match the verifier or the state. |
| `403 cross_origin_rejected` | The exchange was called from a web page. |
| `403 csrf_rejected` | The confirmation came from another site. A token from an earlier browser session opens the confirmation page again instead. |
| `403 user_inactive` | The account is deactivated. |
| `403 tenant_unavailable` | The workspace is unavailable. |
| `426 desktop_app_outdated` | The app is older than `server.desktop_min_version` or names no `app_version`. At the start and on the confirmation page the answer is a page with the header `X-SubKit-Error: desktop_app_outdated`, at the exchange JSON. The sign-in code is not consumed. |
| `429 rate_limit_exceeded` | Too many calls from one address; see `Retry-After`. |

Each entry of `installations` in `GET /v1/cockpit/installations` has `id`, `kind` (`browser` or `desktop`), `device_label` (`null` for the installed web app), `created_at`, `last_used_at` (the last request a session of this installation made, or `null`) and `current` (`true` for the installation the request comes from). A request with the cookie of a revoked installation answers `403 installation_revoked`. `DELETE` from the session of an installation for another installation answers `403 own_installation_only`.

The session of a desktop device lasts 30 days without use and at most 90 days since the sign-in; that of the browser and the installed web app 8 hours without use and at most 24 hours. A revocation ends any of them at once.

### Event stream of the Cockpit

`GET /v1/cockpit/events/stream` sends these frames and fields besides the changes:

| Frame or field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `hello` | First frame with `cursor`, `version` and `heartbeat_ms`. Carries `delivery` while notifications for the person are held back. |
| `ping` | Heartbeat every `heartbeat_ms`. Carries `delivery` like `hello`; a `ping` without the field means announcing is allowed again. |
| `delivery` on a change | `held`: do not announce. `critical_only`: announce only critical items. The list of what needs you and its counter are updated all the same. |
| `server.shutdown` | Last frame when the engine stops. The client shows the state “offline” without an error notice and reconnects with a growing delay. |

The Cockpit announces nothing from the stream; it only updates its lists. SubKit Desktop announces new items as a system notification and follows `delivery`: it reports held items as soon as a frame without `delivery` arrives. When several schedules pause at once, SubKit Desktop and the web push notification fold them into one message, for example “3 schedules were paused”; the push carries `summary.schedules_paused` for that.

The fields of `clients.desktop` in `/.well-known/service-descriptor.json` are described in “Operate the desktop sign-in”.

### Events and attention items

Three event types are new. All three can be used in subscriptions and webhooks, and the `subkit` inbox of a new workspace receives them.

| Event | Sent when | Fields |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `schedule.auto_paused` | A workflow schedule paused itself after five failures in a row. Sent once. | `severity`, `workflow_id`, `workflow_name`, `schedule_id`, `environment`, `paused_reason`, `failure_class`, `consecutive_failures`, `paused_at`, `remedy` |
| `workflow.approval_expiring` | An approval that a schedule or an inbound webhook depends on ends within 3 days. Sent once per approval. | `workflow_id`, `workflow_name`, `authority_id`, `environment`, `valid_until`, `remedy` |
| `task.grant_expiring` | The standing permission of a scheduled task ends within 3 days. Sent once per permission. | `task_id`, `task_name`, `grant_id`, `environment`, `valid_until`, `remedy` |

`remedy` names what helps as `{kind, href}`: `resume` for a paused schedule, `renew` for an approval.

Changes to the attention list at `GET /v1/attention`:

- New reason `schedule_auto_paused`, class `stopped`, with `counts.consecutive_failures`.
- The reasons `approval_expiring` and `task_grant_expiring` now appear 7 days before the end, and the first action of an expiring workflow approval is `renew`.
- `subject.environment` names `dev` or `prod` for connectors.
- `waiting_on` with `user_id` and `name` is set when you named another person as approver.

Changes to the Cockpit event stream at `/v1/cockpit/events/stream`:

- `hello` carries `heartbeat_ms`.
- Events about a connector, a workflow or a task carry `attention_id` with the item they are about.
- `session.ended` with `status` and `code` is the last event when the session of an installation ends.

### Audit actions

| Action | Written when |
| --- | --- |
| `user.setup_updated` | A person changed their setup choices. |
| `tool_approval_rule.created` | A person stored an offered rule. |
| `tool_approval_rule.dismissed` | A person declined an offered rule. |
| `tool_approval_rule.revoked` | A person revoked a rule. |
| `tool_approval_rule.renewed` | A person renewed a rule. |
| `feedback.submitted` | A report was filed. The entry points at the inbox item. |
| `desktop_login.code_issued` | A person confirmed a desktop device in the browser. |
| `desktop_login.denied` | A desktop sign-in was cancelled or its exchange failed. |
| `desktop_login.completed` | The desktop app received its session. |

An action that ran in chat without a question is written as `tool_policy.confirmation_skipped` with the reason `user_instruction` or `standing_rule`. The entry names the verb, the effect, the target, the account, the recipients, a short summary of the content and, for the person’s own words, the quote. A schedule that paused itself is written as `schedule.paused` with the reason `repeated_failures` and the actor `system`.

### Settings

| Setting | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `server.desktop_min_version` | Version such as `12.1.7` | `0.1.0` | Oldest SubKit Desktop version this engine accepts. Published as `clients.desktop.min_version` and enforced by the engine at the desktop sign-in (`426 desktop_app_outdated`). |
| `server.desktop_dev_callback` | `true` or `false` | `false` | Also accept `subkit-dev://callback` as a sign-in target, for development builds. |

Both also appear in the generated settings reference. The thresholds for schedules, rules and notices are fixed and have no setting: backoff from 3 failures, pause at 5, history for 90 days, rules for 90 days with 20 runs a day, before an approval ends a notice in the overview 7 days before, with push also on devices, and a notification through channels and rules 3 days before.
## Reference: pair approval, invitations, offline reports and notification pause

This page lists the routes, fields and audit actions behind four features: two-person workflow approval, sending an invitation, reports that were written offline, and a personal notification pause.
It is for developers and operators who build on them. The task-oriented chapters are “Set SubKit up for yourself”, “Notifications and quiet hours” and “Report a bug”.
The complete, machine-readable description of every route is at `/openapi.json` on your engine.

### Routes

| Route | Who may call it | Does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /v1/workspace/approval-policy` | `workflow:read` | Says whether one person or two people approve a workflow, and how many people may approve. |
| `PUT /v1/workspace/approval-policy` | `rbac:write` | Switches between `single` and `pair`. |
| `POST /v1/workflows/{id}/pair-approvals` | `workflow:write` in a browser session | Records the first of two approvals. |
| `GET /v1/workflows/{id}/pair-approvals` | `workflow:read` | Lists the requests of a workflow, newest first. Optional `state`. |
| `POST /v1/workflows/{id}/pair-approvals/{request_id}/approve` | `workflow:write` in a browser session, not the first approver | Records the second approval. The execution authority exists from now on. |
| `POST /v1/workflows/{id}/pair-approvals/{request_id}/decline` | `workflow:write` in a browser session, not the first approver | Closes the request as declined. |
| `POST /v1/workflows/{id}/pair-approvals/{request_id}/withdraw` | The first approver, or someone with `rbac:write`, in a browser session | Closes the request as withdrawn. |
| `POST /v1/identity/users/{id}/invites/send` | An administrator | Issues a new invitation link for a person who has not joined yet and tries to deliver it. |
| `GET /v1/identity/me/notification-pause` | A person | Reads your pause. |
| `PUT /v1/identity/me/notification-pause` | A person | Pauses your notifications. |
| `DELETE /v1/identity/me/notification-pause` | A person | Resumes your notifications. |
| `POST /v1/feedback` | A person in a browser session | Takes the new field `created_on_device_at` and answers with `replayed`. |

### Pair approval

Under `pair`, an approval only takes effect when two different people with `workflow:write` have both approved the same reviewed boundary: version, effect digest, environment, window and run limit.

- The first approval creates a request, not an execution authority. Nothing may run.
- The execution authority is created only with the second approval. The engine checks the boundary again at that moment.
- One person can never take both places. A second browser session of the same person is the same person.
- While `pair` applies, every way that would let one person approve alone answers `409 pair_approval_required`. That covers `POST /v1/workflows/{id}/execution-authorities`, standing permissions of tasks and `…/until-revoked`.
- The approval card in chat saves the workflow and records the first of two approvals instead. The completed review names the request in `result.pair_request_id`. A schedule cannot be added in the same step: `422 pair_schedule_unsupported`.
- `pair` can only be switched on when at least two active people may approve: `409 pair_needs_two_approvers` with `details.eligible_approvers`. If people leave later, open requests stay open. An administrator switches back to `single` explicitly. There is no silent fallback.

States of a request:

| `state` | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `pending` | Waits for the second person. |
| `approved` | Both approved. `authority_id` names the execution authority. |
| `declined` | The second person declined. |
| `withdrawn` | The first person or an administrator withdrew the request. |
| `expired` | Nobody approved within 72 hours, or before the approval would have ended. |
| `stale` | `stale_reason` is `manifest_changed` (the workflow changed) or `first_approver_unavailable` (the first person can no longer approve). |

Error codes: `pair_same_person` (403), `pair_not_requester` (403), `pair_request_not_found` (404), `pair_not_required`, `pair_request_closed`, `pair_request_expired`, `pair_request_stale`, `authority_manifest_changed` (409) and `pair_start_run_unsupported` (422).

In the setup, `approver: {kind: "pair", email}` names the partner. The answer adds `pair`: `active`, `needs_second_approver` (pair starts once the partner has joined with a role that may approve) or `needs_admin` (an administrator switches it on). Choosing **Me** later does not switch the workspace back.

The attention list shows an open request with the reason `pair_approval_requested` to everyone who may take the second place. The person who asked sees it with `waiting_on` set to the named partner.

### Send an invitation

`POST /v1/identity/users/{id}/invites/send` with an optional `ttl_minutes`. It answers `201`, because a new invitation exists in every case. The previous link stops working.

| `delivery` | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `sent` | The invitation went out by email. `to` shows the address partly masked. |
| `copy_link` | Nothing was sent. `reason` says why: `no_mail_transport`, `mail_failed` or `no_public_url`. The answer carries `plaintext_token`, `link_path` and, when the engine knows its address, `url`. Hand the link over yourself. |

The engine has no mail transport yet, so the answer is `copy_link` with `no_mail_transport`. Further errors: `409 not_invited` (the person has already joined) and `429 rate_limit_exceeded` with `retry_after_seconds` (at most 5 sends per administrator and 2 per invited person within 10 minutes).

### Reports from an offline queue

- `client_request_id` makes a report idempotent. The same id files nothing twice; the answer then carries `replayed: true`. A retry of a report that was already filed never counts against the rate limit.
- `created_on_device_at` is the time the report was written on the device. It is kept as the capture time when it lies within the last 30 days and at most 5 minutes in the future; otherwise the server time counts.
- The queue lives in the client. Both the Cockpit and SubKit Desktop use the same model: one report at a time, retries after 30 seconds, doubling up to 30 minutes; `429` waits as long as the server says; `401` and `403` wait until you sign in again; `409`, `413` and `422` end the attempt. A report is only ever sent for the server and the person it was written for, and is dropped after 14 days.

### Notification pause

Body of `PUT`: `{"mode": "for", "minutes": 60}`, `{"mode": "until", "until": "…"}` or `{"mode": "until_resumed"}`. The end has to lie in the future and at most 30 days ahead, otherwise `422 pause_in_past` or `422 pause_too_long`. The answer is `{paused, mode, paused_at, until}`. A pause that has ended reads as `paused: false`.

During the pause, push notifications and desktop banners are held back. The attention list and the counters keep counting. If you opted into critical items despite quiet hours, they still reach you. On the Cockpit event stream, announcements carry `delivery: held` (or `critical_only`), `held_by: pause` and, for a pause with an end, `held_until`. Quiet hours show up there with `held_by: schedule`. An open stream picks up a change within 30 seconds.

### Audit actions

| Action | Written when |
| --- | --- |
| `workspace.approval_policy_changed` | The workspace switches between `single` and `pair`. `metadata.source` is `policy`, `setup` or `approver_joined`. |
| `workflow.pair_approval_requested` | The first person approves. |
| `workflow.pair_approval_approved` | The second person approves. `workflow.authority_granted` follows. |
| `workflow.pair_approval_declined`, `workflow.pair_approval_withdrawn` | A person closes the request. |
| `workflow.pair_approval_expired`, `workflow.pair_approval_stale` | The engine closes the request. `reason` names the cause for `stale`. |
| `user.invite_delivery` | An invitation was sent or handed back as a link. `reason` is the `copy_link` reason. |
| `user.notifications_paused`, `user.notifications_resumed` | You pause or resume notifications. |
## Reference: files from the desktop, run results and sign-in signals

This page lists what SubKit added so the desktop app and the Cockpit can show files, results and sign-ins without guessing.
It is for developers and operators who build on these parts. The complete, machine-readable description of every route is at `/openapi.json` on your engine.

### Routes

| Route | Who may call it | Does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `POST /v1/chat/composer/attachments` | A person with `conversation:write` | Puts a file into your chat composer. It waits there for your next message. |
| `GET /v1/chat/composer/attachments` | A person with `conversation:read` | Lists the files waiting in your composer, newest first. |
| `POST /v1/chat/composer/attachments/claim` | A person with `conversation:write` | Attaches the waiting files to a conversation and empties the composer. |
| `DELETE /v1/chat/composer/attachments/{id}` | A person with `conversation:write` | Takes one file out of your composer. |
| `POST /v1/intake/items/file` | `intake:write` | Collects a file into the inbox. |

“A person” means a user account, not a system account. A system account gets `403 person_required`.

### Files for your next chat message

The desktop app's drop sheet uses these routes for “Attach in chat”. The Cockpit chat picks the files up when it opens or gets focus.

- The body of `POST` is the same as for a conversation attachment: `{filename, content_type, content_base64}` for a new file, or `{"$file": "<file id>"}` for a file that already exists.
- The answer is `{id, file, staged_at, expires_at}`. `file` has the same fields as a conversation attachment, including `slug` and `reference`.
- A file waits for 24 hours. Your composer holds at most 10 files; one more gets `409 composer_full`. Staging the same file again only renews its time.
- Files are limited to 5 MB and go through the same malware check as every upload.
- Only you see, take or remove your own waiting files. Someone else's id answers `404`.
- `claim` takes `{conversation_id, ids?}`. Without `ids` it takes every waiting file. If one of the `ids` is not waiting in your composer, the whole claim is refused with `404` and nothing changes.

### Files in the inbox

`POST /v1/intake/items/file` takes `{client_request_id, captured_at, filename, content_type, content_base64, category?, title?, note?}`.

| Type | `content_type` |
| --- | --- |
| PDF | `application/pdf` |
| Images | `image/png`, `image/jpeg`, `image/gif`, `image/webp` |
| Text | `text/csv`, `text/plain`, `text/markdown`, `application/json` |

- At most 5 MB.
- The bytes must match the type: a PNG must start like a PNG, text must be UTF-8, JSON must parse. HTML, SVG, XML and scripts are refused, also when they claim to be text.
- The file goes through the malware check. A rejected file creates no item.
- `title` defaults to the filename. The item text is the file's text for CSV, text, Markdown and JSON; for PDFs and images it is one line naming the file.
- `client_request_id` works as with text items: the same id with the same file returns the same item.
- Every intake item now carries `attachment`: `null`, or `{file_id, filename, content_type, size_bytes}`. Download the file with `GET /v1/files/{file_id}/content` (`file:read`).

| Answer | Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 413 | `too_large` | Larger than 5 MB. |
| 422 | `unsupported_file_type` | The type is not in the list. |
| 422 | `content_type_mismatch` | The content does not match the type. |
| 422 | `file_rejected` | The malware check rejected the file. |
| 409 | `conflict` | The `client_request_id` was already used for something else. |

### Markdown result of a run

`GET /v1/executions/{id}` now carries `result_markdown` (text or `null`) and `result_markdown_truncated`. The run detail shows the text as the result of the run.

A workflow provides the result in one of two ways:

1. **Declared:** its `output_schema` marks a text as Markdown with `"contentMediaType": "text/markdown"`, either for the whole output or for one top-level field. If several fields carry the mark, the first one counts.
2. **By name:** without such a mark, a top-level text field `result_markdown` in the output counts.

```json
{
  "output_schema": {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
      "summary": { "type": "string", "contentMediaType": "text/markdown" }
    }
  }
}
```

- The output counts after `output_transform`, so a transform can build the text from the last step.
- Only a succeeded run keeps a result. It is stored once, when the run ends.
- Secrets are removed before it is stored: tokens, keys and passwords become `***redacted***`, and so do credentials in links. Confidential workflows never keep a result.
- At most 64 KiB of text is kept. A longer text is cut and `result_markdown_truncated` is `true`.

### Links to changed records

`GET /v1/executions/{id}`, the MCP tool `get_execution` and `subkit executions show` carry `record_links`: one entry per record that a request step created or changed in an external system, with `label`, `url`, `connector`, `connector_name` and `step_key`. The Cockpit shows them as buttons such as “View in GitHub” that open in a new tab.

- Built-in connector templates declare which requests lead to a record (`record_url_patterns`) and which web hosts are allowed (`web_hosts`). A web address the response already contains is preferred.
- Only `https` addresses on a known web host count. Connectors without a built-in template get no links.
- Confidential runs, held writes and step outputs that were redacted or stored as a file get no links.
- At most 20 links per run, in step order, each address once.

### Outcome of a scheduled run

Every entry of the schedule history (`GET /v1/workflows/{id}/schedule-occurrences`, `GET /v1/tasks/{id}/schedule-occurrences`) now carries `run_outcome`:

| `run_outcome` | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `running` | The run has not ended yet. |
| `succeeded` | The run ended successfully. |
| `failed` | The run failed or ran out of time. |
| `aborted` | The run was stopped. |
| `null` | The entry started no run, or the run is no longer kept. |

`state` keeps describing the timing (on time, late, skipped, held); `run_outcome` says how the run ended.

### Sign-in finished

When a connector sign-in ends, successfully or not, SubKit writes the event `connector.oauth.signin_finished`. This holds for OAuth connectors, MCP connectors and account connections; for an account connection SubKit writes one event per connector that uses it, with `connector_slug` `null`.

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `connector_id` | The connector. |
| `connector_slug` | Its short name, or `null`. |
| `outcome` | `succeeded` or `failed`. |
| `reason` | Why it failed: `provider_error`, `missing_code` or `token_exchange_failed`. `null` on success. |

- On the Cockpit stream (`GET /v1/cockpit/events/stream`, with `connector:read`) the event arrives with `connector_id`, `attention_id`, `outcome` and, on failure, `reason`. The desktop app and the Cockpit wait for it instead of guessing from the window focus.
- Webhook subscriptions can subscribe to it like any other event.
- A sign-in link that expired or is unknown belongs to no connector and writes no event.

### Full stats series

`GET /v1/stats/executions` and `GET /v1/stats/llm` take `fill`:

- `zero` (default): every bucket of the window is listed, oldest first, also the empty ones with `0`. Without `group_by` the answer always has exactly one group.
- `none`: only buckets with data, as before. Useful for wide breakdowns such as `group_by=conversation`.

### Audit actions

| Action | Written when |
| --- | --- |
| `chat.composer_attachment_staged` | A file was put into a composer. |
| `chat.composer_attachment_removed` | A file was taken out of a composer. |
| `chat.composer_attachments_claimed` | Waiting files were attached to a conversation. `file.link_added` follows for each file. |
| `intake_item.collected` | As before; for a file it carries `attachment_file_id`. |
## SubKit features at a glance

This page lists every feature of SubKit in one place, grouped by area, so rarely used ones are easy to find again.
Each line says what you get and links to the chapter that explains it.

### Legend

| Mark | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **All** | Available in SubKit Cloud and on your own engine. |
| **Self-hosted** | Only when you run the engine yourself. |
| **Cloud** | Only in SubKit Cloud. |
| **Admin** | Only people with the Admin role, or the engine operator, can use or change it. |
| **Optional** | Off by default. You or an administrator switch it on. |

### Workflows and runs

| Feature | What you get | Where | More |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Workflow from a sentence | Describe the task in chat, and the AI drafts a workflow you review and save. | All | [Your first workflow](setup.md#your-first-workflow) |
| Fixed steps | A workflow runs request, transform, call, wait, wait for event, branch, parallel and loop steps, the same way every time. | All | [Your first workflow](setup.md#your-first-workflow) |
| Versions | Every change is a new version; the approved version keeps running until a new one is approved. | All | [Your first workflow](setup.md#your-first-workflow) |
| Test and production | Every run and approval belongs to an environment, and the Cockpit labels which one you are in. | All | [Find your way in the Cockpit](setup.md#find-your-way-in-the-cockpit) |
| Trial run | Without an approval, a run is a dry run: writes are held back and nothing is sent. | All | [Connect AI clients via MCP](setup.md#connect-ai-clients-via-mcp) |
| Run result | Every run shows its state, steps, version and why it was allowed, with a link to the audit trail. | All | [Your first workflow](setup.md#your-first-workflow) |
| Markdown result | A run can hand over a written result in Markdown that the Cockpit shows. | All | [Reference: files from the desktop, run results and sign-in signals](setup.md#reference-files-from-the-desktop-run-results-and-sign-in-signals) |
| Fix it in chat | When a step fails or blocks an approval, SubKit suggests a fix in chat that you review again. | All | [Your first workflow](setup.md#your-first-workflow) |
| Automation check | Saving a workflow or schedule tells you whether it can run on its own or which step needs a change. | All | [Use the HTTP API](setup.md#use-the-http-api) |
| Sandbox data tools | Transform steps calculate, parse and validate data with built-in helpers in an isolated sandbox. | All | [Sandbox data tools](setup.md#sandbox-data-tools) |
| Packages | Export workflows, connectors, skills, schedules, sources and files and import them into another engine. | All | [Use the subkit CLI on your machine](setup.md#use-the-subkit-cli-on-your-machine) |

### Approvals and permissions

| Feature | What you get | Where | More |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Approve what it may access | A person approves the environment, the validity and the reads, writes and services before the first real run. | All | [Your first workflow](setup.md#your-first-workflow) |
| Approval until revoked | An approval can stand until revoked or end at a date or after a number of runs. | All | [Your first workflow](setup.md#your-first-workflow) |
| Approval follows a new version | A new version needs no new approval as long as it reaches no further; otherwise SubKit names the difference. | All | [Connect AI clients via MCP](setup.md#connect-ai-clients-via-mcp) |
| Renew before it ends | SubKit reports an approval three days before it ends, and you can renew it. | All | [Keep an eye on schedules](setup.md#keep-an-eye-on-schedules) |
| Two-person approval (“approve together”) | Every workflow approval needs two different people, for teams that must not let one person approve sensitive workflows alone. Off by default; the setting appears only when at least two people in the workspace may approve, and only administrators change it. | Admin · Optional | [Reference: pair approval, invitations, offline reports and notification pause](setup.md#reference-pair-approval-invitations-offline-reports-and-notification-pause) |
| Allow once | A write tool called from an AI client pauses until a person selects **Allow once** or **Decline**. | All | [Connect AI clients via MCP](setup.md#connect-ai-clients-via-mcp) |
| Roles, groups and grants | Roles, permissions and scoped API keys apply the same way to the Cockpit, `subkit`, the API and MCP. | Admin | [Execution identity and permission](setup.md#execution-identity-and-permission) |

## Reference: workflow steps on your device

A workflow can read and write files in folders you allowed on your Mac, work in a website you allowed, and act in an app you allowed. Each such step is an ordinary `request` step on a device connector.
This page lists the step bodies and the rules of the approval. It is for people who write workflows by hand and for developers who build on them.

### Device connectors

When SubKit Desktop is connected and you turn a capability on in Settings › Local capabilities, SubKit creates one connector per capability for that device, for example “MacBook Pro (Mike): Files”, “MacBook Pro (Mike): Browser” and “MacBook Pro (Mike): Computer”. The name uses the language of SubKit Desktop on that device, German or English, and English otherwise. A connector keeps its name when the language changes later. They have the driver `local_files`, `local_browser` or `local_computer`, `config: {device_id}` and no credential.
Bind a step to one of them with `connector_id`. When you disconnect the device, its connectors stay, switched off, so existing workflows show what they used.

### Path and method

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `path` | The action, for example `/files.write`, `/browser.open` or `/computer.type`. |
| `method` | `GET` for an action that only reads, `POST` for an action that changes something. A step whose method does not fit its action is refused before anything is sent. |
| `body` | The fields of the action, directly in `body`. |

Reading actions: `files.list`, `files.read_text`, `browser.snapshot`, `browser.wait`, `browser.extract`, `browser.screenshot`, `computer.apps`, `computer.snapshot`, `computer.screenshot`.

### Files

`folder_id` is the id of a folder you allowed on the device. `path` is relative to that folder.

| Action | Body | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `files.list` | `{folder_id, path?}` | `entries`, `truncated`, `omitted` (at most 500 entries). |
| `files.read_text` | `{folder_id, path}` | `text`, `size`, `sha256` (at most 256 KiB). |
| `files.import` | `{folder_id, path, name?}` | A SubKit file the next steps can use: `file`, `filename`, `content_type`, `size_bytes`, `file_id`, `sha256` (at most 90 MiB). |
| `files.write` | `{folder_id, path, content, replace?}` | `size`, `sha256`, `replaced`, `previous_in_trash`, versions. `content` is text or `{encoding: "base64", data}`; at most 10 MiB. |
| `files.mkdir` | `{folder_id, path}` | – |
| `files.move` | `{folder_id, to_folder_id?, path, to_path}` or `{folder_id, to_folder_id?, items: [{from, to}]}` | One result per item, at most 200. |
| `files.trash` | `{folder_id, path}` or `{folder_id, paths: [...]}` | One result per item, at most 200. |

A move or trash step succeeds only when every item was done. Replaced and removed files go to the Trash. Hidden files, secret files such as keys, and programs are always refused.

### Browser

| Action | Body |
| --- | --- |
| `browser.open` | `{url}` on a website you allowed. |
| `browser.press` | `{action: "click", element}`, `{action: "key", key}` or `{action: "scroll", direction, pixels?}` |
| `browser.fill` | `{mode: "fill" or "type", element, text}` or `{mode: "select", element, values}` |
| `browser.wait` | `{for: "load", state?}`, `{for: "text", text}` or `{for: "ms", ms}` (at most 30 s) |
| `browser.extract` | `{element?}` returns the text of the element or the page. |
| `browser.snapshot`, `browser.screenshot` | `{}` |
| `browser.download` | `{element, folder_id, name}` saves into a folder with write access. |

`browser.pdf` and `browser.handover` are not available in workflows yet.

### Computer

`app_id` is the bundle ID of an app you allowed, for example `com.apple.iWork.Numbers`. SubKit acts in the app's window that has focus, otherwise in its first window.

| Action | Body |
| --- | --- |
| `computer.apps` | `{}` lists the windows of allowed apps. |
| `computer.snapshot`, `computer.screenshot` | `{app_id}` |
| `computer.press`, `computer.focus` | `{app_id, element}` |
| `computer.type` | `{app_id, element, text}` |
| `computer.set_value` | `{app_id, element, value}` |
| `computer.select` | `{app_id, element, option}` |
| `computer.scroll` | `{app_id, element, direction, amount}` |
| `computer.key` | `{app_id, keys}`, for example `"cmd+s"` |

### Elements

Name an element as `element: {role, name, nth?}`, for example `{role: "button", name: "Download"}`. `nth` picks among several elements with the same role and name, starting at 0. Refs like `e12` are not allowed in a workflow: they change with every snapshot. SubKit takes a fresh snapshot right before each such action and finds the element there. If no element or more than one element matches, the step fails with `element_not_found` or `element_ambiguous` and nothing is changed.

### Screenshots

A screenshot is redacted on the device: password fields and fields marked as sensitive are blacked out. The step result keeps only `screenshot_ref`, the SHA-256 of the PNG. The image itself is kept encrypted with the device's answer for 30 days and then deleted.

### Approval and growth

- The approval names the device and, for each local step, the folders with read or write access, the websites and the apps the step uses. An import only reads its folder.
- Write `folder_id`, `to_folder_id`, `url` and `app_id` as fixed values. A placeholder there leaves the workflow unapprovable. A value that is only filled in while the run goes and that the approval does not name is refused with `outside_boundary`.
- A workflow with a device is approved on that device.
- A new version needs a new approval when it adds a folder, needs write access where reading was approved, adds a website or private address, or adds an app. Fewer items carry the approval forward.
- Browser and computer steps run only for the device's person: from their chat or task, a run they start, or a schedule they set up.
- A workflow that another workflow calls refuses local steps. Keep local steps in the workflow you approve and run.

### Errors

| Code | Means |
| --- | --- |
| `outside_boundary` | The step goes beyond the approval. Review and approve it again on the device. |
| `outside_allowance`, `origin_not_allowed`, `private_address` | The device does not allow this folder, website or app. |
| `folder_changed` | The allowed folder was replaced. Allow it again and renew the approval. |
| `permission_missing` | A macOS permission is missing (Accessibility or Screen Recording). |
| `kind_not_ready` | This action is not available in workflows yet. |
| `local_method_mismatch`, `local_step_invalid` | Method or body do not fit the action. |
| `files_partly_done` | Not every item of a move or trash was done; the result lists each item. |
| `screenshot_unverified` | The screenshot does not match its hash. It was not kept. |

Every error comes with a remedy in `guidance`.
## Reference: the vault

The vault is the one place for every secret in your workspace: API keys, logins and the credentials of your connectors.
A workflow names an item only by its handle. SubKit fills in the value when an approved run executes the step. The AI never sees it.

### What the vault holds

| Kind | For | Fields |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Secret | an API key or token that several workflows need | `token` |
| Login | a username and a password | `username`, `password` |
| Connector credential | a connector's credential, created when you connect it | depends on the sign-in type |
| Template client | the OAuth client of a connector template | `client_id`, `client_secret` |

You add and change secrets and logins in the vault. You change connector credentials and template clients on the connector. The vault shows them and lets you reveal or delete them.

Every item has a name of lowercase letters, digits, `-` and `_`, for example `crm-token`. The name is also the handle. It applies per environment: `crm-token` in test and `crm-token` in production are two items.

### Who an item is for

| Scope | Who sees it | When its value is filled in |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Workspace | everyone with `vault:read`, metadata only | in every approved run of the workspace |
| Only me | only you | only in runs you start |
| This device | only SubKit Desktop on this device | never in workflows; it stays on the device |

SubKit Desktop creates device items itself, for example the key the device uses to identify itself to the server. They are encrypted in the operating system's secure storage and never leave the device.

### Use an item in a workflow

Write the handle into a header, a query value or the body of a request step that has a connector:

```json
{
  "id": "contacts",
  "kind": "request",
  "connector_id": "<crm-connector-id>",
  "method": "GET",
  "path": "/contacts",
  "headers": { "authorization": "Bearer ${secret.crm-token}" },
  "query": { "account": "${secret.crm-account}" },
  "boundary": { "variables": {}, "max_body_bytes": 0, "max_calls": 1 }
}
```

| Form | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `${secret.crm-token}` | the token of a workspace secret |
| `${secret.erp.username}`, `${secret.erp.password}` | the fields of a login |
| `${secret.me.crm-token}` | your own “Only me” item |

These rules always apply:

- **The approval names the items.** It shows “Uses from the vault: crm-token, …” and binds the names, never the values. A new version that uses another item needs a new approval. Fewer items carry the approval forward.
- **Approved runs only.** In drafts, test runs and held steps the handle stays unresolved (`secret_withheld`) and nothing is sent.
- **Own connector only.** A step that carries a vault value may only go to its connector's origin. Any other address stops with `credential_boundary_violation` before anything is sent.
- **Headers, query and body only.** In the path, the URL, a GraphQL query or an MCP call a handle is never resolved; in the path or URL the step stops before anything is sent.
- **The same rules everywhere.** A handle in the query or body is resolved, redacted and approved exactly like one in a header. A query value may hold fixed text around a handle but no other placeholder; the approval checks that the key is sent, not its value, so a rotation needs no new approval.
- **A missing item fails the step** with `placeholder_unresolved`, and nothing is sent.

### What the AI and the records see

The AI, chat, MCP and the subkit CLI get the name, kind, scope, environment, version and last use, never the value.
A run's result, error message, log and audit trail do not contain the value. SubKit replaces it, also URL- or JSON-encoded, with `***redacted***`.

### Rotation

**Replace value** in the vault or `subkit vault rotate` stores a new value and raises the version. The next run uses it. The workflow's approval stays valid, because it binds the handle, not the value.
You rotate the engine's master key (`MASTER_KEY`) with the rewrap maintenance, as before.

### Reveal and activity

**Reveal** shows you the value for a short time, and `subkit vault reveal <id> --yes` prints it in the terminal. Every reveal is in the audit trail.
An item's activity shows when it was created, used, revealed, rotated or deleted. A use names its run and step.

### Permissions

| Permission | Default | Allows |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `vault:read` | all roles | seeing workspace items, without values |
| `vault:write` | admin | adding items and describing them |
| `vault:rotate` | admin | replacing values |
| `vault:delete` | admin | deleting items |
| `vault:reveal` | admin | revealing the values of workspace items |

You always manage your own “Only me” items, even without these permissions.

### In the Cockpit, with subkit and over MCP

- **Cockpit:** Settings › Vault.
- **subkit:** `subkit vault list`, `show`, `add`, `rotate`, `reveal`, `refresh`, `rm`, `attach` and `connector`. `add` and `rotate` read the value from stdin or a hidden prompt, never from arguments.
- **MCP:** `list_vault_items` and `get_vault_item` return metadata only.
- **HTTP:** `/v1/vault`, see the HTTP API.

### Backup and moving

A server backup needs the database and the `MASTER_KEY`. Without it the values cannot be opened.
A package or a move to another workspace takes names and metadata only, never values. There is no plain-text export.

<!-- Source: coding-agents.md -->

# Use SubKit from a coding agent

This chapter is for developers who work with Claude Code, Codex or Hermes.
You give your agent the SubKit tools and, for each repository, a briefing from your team's shared knowledge.
Afterwards the agent runs approved workflows, knows the project's house rules and puts what it learned into your inbox for review.

### Why a coding agent plus SubKit

Your coding agent stays the tool for software: reading, changing and testing code.
Recurring business work needs more than a script: permissions, approvals, history, schedules and safely stored credentials. SubKit carries that.
To the agent, SubKit is a tool: it calls an approved workflow instead of holding credentials itself.
Every call goes through the same permission check as in the Cockpit and appears in the history.

Collected material always follows one path: **collect → review with your agent → confirm in the Cockpit → knowledge**.

### What you need

- The subkit CLI, signed in to your engine. In the cloud, use `subkit login --engine-url https://subkit-cloud.mikebild.dev` and **Sign in with work account**. The briefing uses this signed-in profile.
- The MCP address of your engine, `https://<your-engine>/mcp`. On SubKit Cloud it is `https://subkit-cloud.mikebild.dev/mcp`.
- Claude Code, Codex or Hermes.
- A repository where the briefings should appear.

### Set up the SubKit tools once per machine

1. In the Cockpit, open **API access** and create a key.
2. Store the key in `SUBKIT_API_KEY`.
3. Register SubKit in your client with the matching command.

Claude Code:

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http --scope user subkit https://<your-engine>/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer ${SUBKIT_API_KEY}"
```

Codex:

```bash
codex mcp add subkit --url https://<your-engine>/mcp --bearer-token-env-var SUBKIT_API_KEY
```

A key without `mcp:authoring` lets the agent read and run workflows but build nothing. If it should draft workflows and connectors, create the key with `subkit apikeys create --scopes …,mcp:authoring`.
To sign in without a key, see "Connect AI clients via MCP".

### Set up briefings in a repository

1. In the repository, declare the domains:

   ```bash
   subkit agent init --domains <category>
   ```

   For several domains, separate them with commas: `--domains <category>[,<category>]`.
   The command writes `.subkit/agent.json` and adds the SubKit hooks to `~/.claude/settings.json` and `~/.codex/hooks.json`. Other tools' hooks stay in place.
2. Commit `.subkit/agent.json` so every checkout uses the same domains.
3. In Claude Code or Codex, run `/hooks` and check that the SubKit hooks are active.
4. Trust new or changed SubKit hooks.

### Set up Hermes by hand

For Hermes, `subkit agent init` sets up no hooks. The command's output shows what you need under "Hermes (manual)".

1. In Hermes, register an MCP server over streamable HTTP with the address `https://<your-engine>/mcp`.
2. Pass the header `Authorization: Bearer ${SUBKIT_API_KEY}`.
3. At the start of a session, run `subkit agent briefing` in the repository and hand the output to Hermes as context.

### Check the briefing

1. In the repository, run `subkit status`.
2. Run `subkit agent briefing --json`.
3. Check the fields `domains`, `knowledge_sources`, `skills_full` and `used_tokens`.

### Review collected material with your coding agent

Your agent can start a review of collected entries. You confirm the result in the Cockpit.

1. Ask your agent: "Review the new entries in Research. Which are useful? Propose what we should keep as knowledge."
2. Open the Cockpit link the agent returns. It leads to the item's **Review** tab.
3. Check the proposal's sources, exact text and knowledge destination.
4. Select **Confirm as source**.
5. Run `subkit agent briefing --json` and check `knowledge_sources`.

A new session loads the updated briefing.

Good to know:

- Only a signed-in person with `intake:confirm` and `knowledge:write` confirms a proposal. An API key, an MCP client or the Web Clipper never does.
- The item's original stays linked to the knowledge it became.
- Moving, editing or discarding an entry never admits it as knowledge.

### Review collected material in the terminal

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `subkit intake list` | Shows collected items in your default category. |
| `subkit intake list --category research` | Shows collected items of one category. |
| `subkit intake review --category research` | Starts the review and prints the Cockpit link. |
| `subkit intake review --items <comma-separated-ids>` | Reviews only particular entries. |
| `subkit intake default --category research` | Changes your personal default category. |
| `subkit intake move --item <id> --category research` | Moves an entry to a category. |
| `subkit intake discard --item <id>` | Discards an entry. |
| `subkit intake restore --item <id>` | Restores a discarded entry. |

- Without a selection, `review` uses your default category.
- `--json` returns machine-readable results.
- These actions preserve the item's original and never admit knowledge.

### How briefings work

**Domains.** A domain is a catalog category or a `domain:<slug>` tag.

- `subkit agent init` adds the requested domains and removes nothing that exists.
- Without `.subkit/agent.json`, the hooks match the folder name against your project categories. On a unique match they create `.subkit/agent.json` for you. Otherwise they ask instead of guessing.
- To fix the domains yourself, edit `domains` in `.subkit/agent.json` and remove `inferred` and `inferred_folder_domain`.
- A prompt can add other matching domains as the task changes.

**Hooks.** `init` sets up the SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit and SessionEnd hooks for Claude Code and Codex. `--skip-claude` and `--skip-codex` leave that client's settings untouched.

**Size.** A briefing has at most 1,800 tokens and 9,500 characters, shared by both clients and the interactive subkit session.
Whatever does not fit is shortened, and you see a warning.

A briefing contains:

- Domain context and a short status, with blocked work and deadlines first.
- Up to three specific next steps in your language.
- Matching sources and workflows of the folder's domain, named when they help with a task.
- The number of collected pages and session learnings, never their content. With `intake:read`, also the workspace-wide number of collected entries and pending proposals.

**Session learnings.** At session end, Claude Code and Codex send the transcript to the engine.

- The engine keeps only practices and facts a person taught or confirmed.
- It drops events, status updates and anything credential-related.
- The rest lands in the Inbox with origin `session`, in the project's shared category or your default category. A repeated learning adds evidence to the existing entry.
- Learnings are not knowledge and not skills until a person confirms them in the Cockpit. `subkit intake list` shows what is waiting.

**Reviews with an agent.** The review runs in a saved SubKit conversation.

- MCP clients start it with `conversation_start`. `intake_item_ids` selects particular items and keeps that selection fixed.
- Tools that read entries or prepare proposals work only inside this conversation.
- For a new destination, include the topic category or `domain:<slug>` tag in the proposal. A changed proposal must be reviewed again.

### If something does not work

| What you see | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| `subkit agent briefing: no domains …` | There is no declaration. Pass `--domains` or run `subkit agent init --domains <category>`. |
| `knowledge_sources` or `skills_full` are empty | The briefing works but nothing is assigned to the domain. Put knowledge and skills in the domain's category or use the `domain:<slug>` tag. |
| The client shows a briefing warning | The engine cannot be reached. The session continues. Check sign-in and connection with `subkit status`. |
| No briefings in Claude Code or Codex | Open `/hooks`, check that the SubKit hooks are active, and trust new or changed hooks. |
| `/hooks` in Codex shows the SubKit hooks as disabled | Codex hooks are on by default, so no `config.toml` edit is normally needed. Check the effective feature setting and your administrator policy first, then follow the [Codex hooks guide](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/hooks). |
| The agent cannot draft anything | Its key has no `mcp:authoring`. Create a new key with that scope. |
| The reminder about collected entries is missing | You lack the `intake:read` permission. Ask an administrator for it. |
| A proposal cannot be confirmed | Only a signed-in person with `intake:confirm` and `knowledge:write` can confirm, not an API key. Open the Cockpit link. |

<!-- Source: cli.md -->

# subkit CLI reference

Look up every `subkit` command and argument here. Creating or changing a
workflow, connector, knowledge source or skill also runs through `subkit`:
the change is a file you can read and a command you can re-run.

Bare `subkit` opens an interactive prompt. Every command below also runs in
scripts and prints to stdout. `create --file`, `update --file`, `validate`,
`preview` and `probe` check a definition *before* it is saved. A mistake
then costs an error message, not a half-built connector someone has to
clean up.

The `requires` column names the permission that shows a command in
`--help`. The engine checks permissions again on every API call.

| command | requires | description | subcommands |
| ------- | -------- | ----------- | ----------- |
| `subkit agent` | `skill:read` | Coding-agent integration: session briefings and hook setup | `briefing`, `capture`, `init`, `migrate-hooks` |
| `subkit apikeys` | `api_key:read` | Manage API keys | `create`, `list`, `revoke`, `rotate` |
| `subkit apps` | `settings:read` | The apps that sign their users in and call SubKit (products settings, sign-in providers, workflows, users, budget); erase-user removes one app user's SubKit data | `erase-user`, `list`, `show` |
| `subkit attach` | `file:write` | Upload a file and link it to a conversation (shortcut) | — |
| `subkit audit` | `audit:read` | Query the append-only audit log | `export`, `query`, `show` |
| `subkit auth` | `connector:write` | Start a connector's browser sign-in and print the URL to open. Works for every connector that signs in with an account — a web service or an MCP server; the engine names the route. | — |
| `subkit branding` | — | Read, update, reset, or download tenant branding | `get`, `logo`, `reset`, `update` |
| `subkit categories` | `workflow:read` | Show and rename the catalog categories shared by every kind | `list`, `rename` |
| `subkit chat` | `chat_workspace:read` | Manage external chat spaces (Google Chat / Slack) | `install-space`, `remove-space`, `spaces` |
| `subkit clipper` | — | Install the Chrome clipping extension | `install` |
| `subkit connector-templates` | `connector:read` | Manage connector templates | `create`, `delete`, `list`, `recipe`, `recipe-pack`, `recipes`, `search`, `set-oauth` |
| `subkit connectors` | `connector:read` | Manage connectors | `create`, `delete`, `disable`, `docs-delete`, `docs-ingest`, `docs-list`, `docs-search`, `enable`, `get`, `import`, `inspect`, `list`, `mcp-authorize`, `mcp-inspect`, `patch`, `probe`, `promote`, `test`, `validate` |
| `subkit diagnostics` | `audit:read` | Engine diagnostics: errors, LLM status, setup validation | `errors`, `llm`, `setup` |
| `subkit discovery` | `discovery:read` | Manage discovery runs and artifacts | `approve`, `artifacts`, `create`, `get`, `list`, `reject` |
| `subkit doctor` | — | Diagnose engine connectivity, authentication, and setup. Exits 0 (ok or warn) or 2 (blocked). | — |
| `subkit events` | `audit:read` | Query audit events | `get`, `list` |
| `subkit executions` | `execution:read` | Manage workflow executions | `abort`, `get`, `list`, `rerun`, `result`, `show`, `steps`, `tail` |
| `subkit extract` | `conversation:write` | Extract structured data from a file (LLM for text, native parsers for binary) | — |
| `subkit files` | `file:read` | Manage files (upload, download, link, …) | `delete`, `download`, `get`, `link`, `list`, `patch`, `replace`, `restore`, `stats`, `upload`, `versions` |
| `subkit health` | — | Runtime posture: liveness, token budget, failing runs, risk signals, schema drift, and process runtime. Use `subkit doctor` for connectivity/setup. | — |
| `subkit hooks` | `inbound_hook:read` | Manage inbound webhook bindings | `create`, `delete`, `get`, `list` |
| `subkit init` | — | Complete first-run engine bootstrap (consumes the token printed at engine boot) | — |
| `subkit install` | `connector:write` | Guided setup for enterprise integrations | `github`, `google-workspace`, `hubspot`, `jira`, `salesforce`, `slack` |
| `subkit intake` | `intake:read` | List collected items and start a selected Chat review | `default`, `discard`, `list`, `move`, `restore`, `review` |
| `subkit invites` | `identity:read` | Manage user-provisioning invites | `list`, `revoke` |
| `subkit join` | — | Redeem an invite to provision your personal API key (no login required) | — |
| `subkit knowledge-sources` | `knowledge:read` | Manage knowledge sources | `analyze`, `create`, `delete`, `get`, `history`, `import`, `list`, `patch`, `restore`, `search` |
| `subkit login` | — | Authenticate against a subkit engine | — |
| `subkit logout` | — | Drop the active profile | — |
| `subkit logs` | `audit:read` | Tail the engine's runtime log ring. --follow streams via SSE; --since accepts 5m / 2h / 1d / ISO-8601. | — |
| `subkit ls` | — | List cached conversation sessions for the active profile | — |
| `subkit mcp` | — | Run a stdio MCP server proxied to the engine | — |
| `subkit notifications` | `notification:read` | Manage notification channels, rules, deliveries, and the inbox | `channels`, `deliveries`, `inbox`, `rules` |
| `subkit packages` | `package:import` | Move this workspace to another engine: export a package archive, import one with a reviewed plan, list past imports | `export`, `import`, `installs` |
| `subkit patch-candidates` | `workflow:read` | Manage patch candidates | `approve`, `get`, `list`, `preview`, `reject` |
| `subkit portal-tokens` | `portal_token:read` | Manage portal tokens | `create`, `list`, `revoke` |
| `subkit profile` | — | Manage named profiles (environments) | `add`, `delete`, `list`, `show`, `use` |
| `subkit rbac` | `rbac:read` | Manage RBAC roles, permissions, grants, groups, and hooks | `can`, `grants`, `groups`, `permissions`, `request-hooks`, `roles`, `users`, `whatcan` |
| `subkit rename` | — | Assign or change a short alias for a session (used by `subkit -r <alias>`) | — |
| `subkit review` | `workflow:read` | Aggregated approval digest: pending patch candidates, proposed skill candidates, and recent failed executions. | — |
| `subkit rm` | — | Drop a session from the local cache (the server-side conversation row is preserved) | — |
| `subkit schedules` | `workflow:read` | Scheduled workflow runs | `create`, `delete`, `list`, `pause`, `resume`, `update` |
| `subkit self-healing` | `workflow:write` | Trigger and review proactive drift scans (admin) | `list`, `scan`, `show` |
| `subkit sessions` | — | Manage locally-cached conversation sessions | `ls`, `rename`, `rm`, `search`, `show` |
| `subkit settings` | `settings:read` | List, read, write, or interactively configure engine settings (secrets always masked) | `configure`, `get`, `list`, `set` |
| `subkit show` | — | Show cached metadata for a session by id or alias | — |
| `subkit skill-candidates` | `skill:read` | Manage skill candidates | `approve`, `get`, `list`, `reject` |
| `subkit skills` | `skill:read` | Manage skills | `activate`, `archive`, `create`, `delete`, `edit`, `get`, `history`, `list`, `patch`, `restore`, `sync` |
| `subkit stats` | `stats:read` | Tenant-scoped runtime statistics (needs stats:read) | `chat`, `connectors`, `conversations`, `events`, `executions`, `http`, `llm`, `mcp`, `operations` |
| `subkit status` | — | Print the active profile + engine reachability | — |
| `subkit subscriptions` | `subscription:read` | Manage event subscriptions | `create`, `delete`, `deliveries`, `get`, `list`, `patch`, `replay` |
| `subkit system` | `system:restart` | Engine process operations (restart) | `restart` |
| `subkit system-accounts` | `identity:read` | Manage system accounts | `create`, `delete`, `list` |
| `subkit tasks` | `task:read` | Tasks: a goal with limits that works on its own and asks before it acts | `abort`, `create`, `delete`, `get`, `list`, `pause`, `resume`, `run`, `runs`, `update` |
| `subkit tenants` | — | List tenants you belong to or switch the active one | — |
| `subkit update` | — | Update the subkit CLI to the latest release, or to the version of your engine | — |
| `subkit users` | `identity:read` | Manage identity users | `create`, `delete`, `get`, `invite`, `list`, `patch` |
| `subkit vault` | — | The vault (Tresor): secrets, logins and connector credentials. Workflows name an item as ${secret.<name>}; values never reach the model. | `add`, `attach`, `connector`, `list`, `refresh`, `reveal`, `rm`, `rotate`, `show` |
| `subkit workflows` | `workflow:read` | Manage workflows | `create`, `delete`, `dry-run`, `get`, `history`, `invoke-snippet`, `list`, `patch`, `preview`, `restore`, `run`, `update`, `validate` |

## Commands and arguments

Every argument of every command. `<name>` is positional; `--name` is a flag.

### `subkit agent`

Coding-agent integration: session briefings and hook setup

#### `subkit agent briefing`

Print or verify the domain-scoped session briefing for coding agents

- `--domains` (string) — Comma-separated domain slugs (default: .subkit/agent.json of the repo; without hooks, else the known domains the repository name names)
- `--budget` (string) — Token budget for the briefing
- `--hook` (default: false) — Hook mode for Codex and Claude Code: inject a repository briefing and show a non-blocking status or warning
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `subkit agent capture`

Send a session transcript to the engine to collect learnings for review

- `--transcript` (string) — Path to the transcript file (JSONL or text)
- `--domains` (string) — Comma-separated domain slugs (default: .subkit/agent.json of the repo)
- `--agent` (string, default: claude-code) — Producing agent name
- `--session-id` (string) — Session id for evidence attribution
- `--hook` (default: false) — SessionEnd/Stop-hook mode: read hook JSON from stdin, never fail
- `--detach` (default: false) — Process the hook payload in a detached process
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `subkit agent init`

Set up automatic SubKit briefings for this repository in Claude Code and Codex

- `--domains` (string, required) — Comma-separated domains for this repository (e.g. accounting, blog-de)
- `--budget` (string) — Optional token budget for each briefing
- `--skip-claude` (default: false) — Do not touch ~/.claude/settings.json
- `--skip-codex` (default: false) — Do not touch ~/.codex/hooks.json

#### `subkit agent migrate-hooks`

Rewrite Claude Code and Codex hooks installed for the former `sk` binary to `subkit`

_No arguments._


### `subkit apikeys`

Manage API keys

#### `subkit apikeys create`

Issue a new API key (shown once)

- `--name` (string) — Friendly key name (label)
- `--expires` (string) — Expiry — ISO-8601 timestamp
- `--scopes` (string) — Comma-separated scope strings (e.g. "workflow:read,workflow:run"). Defaults to your own credential's scopes; ["*"] (full role-derived access, and read-and-execute over MCP) only when your credential has no scope limits. Add "mcp:authoring" for a key that may also author definitions over MCP (a coding agent); leave it off for a key going into a browser client.
- `--allowed-workflows` (string) — Comma-separated workflow ids/slugs. Use "*" for explicit "all".
- `--allowed-connectors` (string) — Comma-separated connector ids/slugs. Use "*" for explicit "all".

#### `subkit apikeys list`

List API keys

- `--json` — JSON output

#### `subkit apikeys revoke`

Revoke an API key

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Key id

#### `subkit apikeys rotate`

Rotate an API key (new key shown once)

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Key id


### `subkit apps`

The apps that sign their users in and call SubKit (products settings, sign-in providers, workflows, users, budget); erase-user removes one app user's SubKit data

#### `subkit apps erase-user`

Erase an app user: removes SubKit's own data about that person for this app; the account at the sign-in provider stays. Irreversible

- `<app>` (positional, required) — App id (the product_id)
- `<user>` (positional, required) — User id (listed by subkit apps show <app>)
- `--yes` (default: false) — Confirm the erasure without asking
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `subkit apps list`

List the apps of this workspace with environment, users, budget today and readiness

- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `subkit apps show`

Show one app: settings, sign-in, workflows, users, today's budget and readiness with the next action

- `<id>` (positional, required) — App id (the product_id)
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output


### `subkit attach`

Upload a file and link it to a conversation (shortcut)

- `<conversation-id>` (positional, required) — Conversation id (UUID)

- `--content-type` (string) — Override detected MIME type
- `--slug` (string) — Optional slug for the link

### `subkit audit`

Query the append-only audit log

#### `subkit audit export`

Stream audit log as NDJSON to stdout or a file

- `--since` (string) — Lower bound — ISO-8601 timestamp
- `--to` (string) — Exclusive UTC upper bound (ISO-8601)
- `--action` (string) — Action name filter
- `--actor` (string) — Actor id filter
- `--actor-type` (string) — Actor kind
- `--api-key-id` (string) — Recorded API key id
- `--session-id` (string) — Recorded session id
- `--access-type` (string) — Verified access type
- `--oauth-client-id` (string) — Verified OAuth client id
- `--request-source` (string) — Legacy recorded source (not verified)
- `--origin-source` (string) — Verified initiating source
- `--execution-source` (string) — Immediate server execution step
- `--correlation-id` (string) — Trusted audit correlation id
- `--resource-type` (string) — Resource type
- `--resource-types` (string) — Comma-separated resource types
- `--resource-id` (string) — Resource id
- `--result` (string) — success, denied or error
- `--trace-id` (string) — Trace id
- `--execution-id` (string) — Recorded execution id
- `--conversation-id` (string) — Recorded conversation id
- `--workflow-id` (string) — Recorded workflow id
- `--output` (string) — Output file path (default: stdout)

#### `subkit audit query`

Filter the audit log

- `--limit` (string) — Max rows
- `--since` (string) — Lower bound — ISO-8601 timestamp or relative (e.g. 10m, 1h, 7d)
- `--action` (string) — Action name filter
- `--actor` (string) — Actor id filter
- `--actor-type` (string) — Actor kind
- `--api-key-id` (string) — Recorded API key id
- `--session-id` (string) — Recorded session id
- `--access-type` (string) — Verified access type
- `--oauth-client-id` (string) — Verified OAuth client id
- `--request-source` (string) — Legacy recorded source (not verified)
- `--origin-source` (string) — Verified initiating source
- `--execution-source` (string) — Immediate server execution step
- `--correlation-id` (string) — Trusted audit correlation id
- `--resource-type` (string) — Resource type
- `--resource-types` (string) — Comma-separated resource types
- `--resource-id` (string) — Filter by resource id
- `--result` (string) — success, denied or error
- `--trace-id` (string) — Trace id
- `--execution-id` (string) — Recorded execution id
- `--conversation-id` (string) — Recorded conversation id
- `--workflow-id` (string) — Recorded workflow id
- `--to` (string) — Exclusive UTC upper bound (ISO-8601)
- `--cursor` (string) — Continue after a previous page (its next_cursor)
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `subkit audit show`

Fetch one audit event by id

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Audit event id
