### `subkit connectors`

Manage connectors

#### `subkit connectors create`

Create a connector from a template slug (--template) or a definition file (--file). --file runs validate and probe against the unsaved definition first, so a broken connector is never created; pass --skip-checks to bypass.

- `--template` (string) — Template slug
- `--file` (string) — Path to a connector definition JSON file
- `--credential` (string) — Path to a credential JSON file used to sign the pre-save probe. Never stored — attach the credential with `subkit vault attach` after create.
- `--name` (string) — Override connector name (--template only)
- `--skip-checks` — Skip the checks (NOT recommended).
- `--json` — JSON-only output (suppresses narration)

#### `subkit connectors delete`

Delete a connector

- `<id>` (positional) — Connector id
- `--yes` — Skip confirmation

#### `subkit connectors disable`

Disable a connector. It keeps its configuration and credentials and stops being offered for use.

- `<id>` (positional) — Connector id

#### `subkit connectors docs-delete`

Delete a connector doc

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Connector id
- `<doc-id>` (positional, required) — Doc id

#### `subkit connectors docs-ingest`

Ingest docs from a URL into a connector

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Connector id
- `--url` (string, required) — URL to ingest
- `--source-type` (string, required) — Document format: openapi | google_discovery | markdown | llms_txt

#### `subkit connectors docs-list`

List ingested docs for a connector

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Connector id
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `subkit connectors docs-search`

Ranked search over connector docs

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Connector id
- `<query>` (positional, required) — Search query
- `--limit` (string, default: 10) — Max results

#### `subkit connectors enable`

Enable a connector (operator on switch)

- `<id>` (positional) — Connector id

#### `subkit connectors get`

Get a connector by id

- `<id>` (positional) — Connector id

#### `subkit connectors import`

Turn an API specification into a connector. Parses the spec, shows the draft it produced, then creates it after confirmation (--yes to skip). Nothing is saved until you agree.

- `--spec` (string, required) — Path to the specification file, or a URL / curl command (see --source)
- `--source` (string, required) — openapi | google_discovery | postman | har | graphql | graphql_introspection | curl
- `--name` (string) — Override the connector name
- `--environment` (string) — dev (default) or prod
- `--yes` — Create without asking (for non-interactive use)
- `--dry-run` — Print the draft and stop. Nothing is created.
- `--json` — JSON-only output

#### `subkit connectors inspect`

Inspect a connector resource (alias of `get`).

- `<id>` (positional) — Connector id

#### `subkit connectors list`

List connectors, grouped into catalog blocks

- `--limit` (string, default: 50) — Max rows
- `--category` (string) — Only this catalog block
- `--driver` (string) — Only this driver: http, graphql, postgres, s3, mcp, local_files, local_browser, local_computer
- `--flat` — One flat table instead of grouped blocks
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `subkit connectors mcp-authorize`

mcp driver: begin the interactive OAuth 2.1 flow and print the URL to open in a browser.

- `<id>` (positional) — Connector id

#### `subkit connectors mcp-inspect`

mcp driver: force one handshake and list the tools, capabilities and instructions the remote actually serves.

- `<id>` (positional) — Connector id

#### `subkit connectors patch`

Update a connector, from --file (a partial definition: only the fields it names change) or from --name, --description and --category. --file runs validate first.

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Connector id
- `--file` (string) — Path to a partial definition JSON file
- `--name` (string) — New name
- `--description` (string) — What it is for, in plain language — the assistant reads this to pick the right object. "" hands it back to automatic description.
- `--category` (string) — Catalog block, lowercase words joined by dashes (see `subkit categories list`). "" hands it back to automatic categorisation.
- `--skip-checks` — Skip validation (NOT recommended).
- `--json` — JSON-only output (suppresses narration)

#### `subkit connectors probe`

Probe a connector's upstream boundary. With an id, probes the saved connector (alias of `test`); with --file, probes an unsaved definition and saves nothing.

- `<id>` (positional) — Connector id
- `--file` (string) — Path to a connector definition JSON file — probes it without saving it
- `--credential` (string) — Path to a credential JSON file. Signs this probe only; never stored. Required when the definition's auth_type is not 'none'.
- `--json` — JSON-only output

#### `subkit connectors promote`

Promote a connector and its credentials from DEV to PROD

- `<id>` (positional) — DEV connector id
- `--to` (string, default: prod) — Target environment (prod only)
- `--strategy` (string, default: copy) — Promotion strategy: copy or move
- `--idempotency-key` (string) — Stable retry key; generated when omitted
- `--yes` — Confirm a move without prompting
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `subkit connectors test`

Test a connector connection (alias of `probe`). Exits non-zero when the probe fails.

- `<id>` (positional) — Connector id
- `--json` — JSON-only output

#### `subkit connectors validate`

Check a connector definition file against its driver's config schema. Saves nothing, reaches no upstream.

- `<file>` (positional, required) — Path to a definition JSON file
- `--json` — JSON-only output

- `--api-key` (string) — Override the resolved API key
- `--profile` (string) — Use a named profile
- `--json` — Emit one JSON object instead of human output

### `subkit executions`

Manage workflow executions

#### `subkit executions abort`

Abort a running execution

- `<id>` (positional) — Execution id

#### `subkit executions get`

Get an execution by id

- `<id>` (positional) — Execution id
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON-only (skip Output files line)

#### `subkit executions list`

List executions

- `--limit` (string, default: 20) — Max rows
- `--status` (string) — Filter by status
- `--source` (string) — Filter by request source (e.g. scheduler, cli, api, mcp, chat)
- `--parent` (string) — Lineage filter: list the reruns spawned from this execution id
- `--from` (string) — Only runs that started at or after this instant (ISO-8601 or now-24h, now-7d, startOfMonth)
- `--to` (string) — Only runs that started before this instant (exclusive; default: open)
- `--cursor` (string) — Continue after a previous page (the next_cursor it printed)
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `subkit executions rerun`

Re-run a previous execution against the workflow + input it carried. Useful after diagnose/repair.

- `<id>` (positional) — Execution id to rerun
- `--input` (string) — Override the original input (JSON string). Omit to reuse it verbatim.
- `--follow` — Queue the rerun and stream its progress live (step-by-step JSON lines).

#### `subkit executions result`

Print the final output a workflow execution produced

- `<id>` (positional) — Execution id
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON-only output

#### `subkit executions show`

Get an execution by id

- `<id>` (positional) — Execution id
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON-only (skip Output files line)

#### `subkit executions steps`

List steps for an execution

- `<id>` (positional) — Execution id
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `subkit executions tail`

Stream live output from an execution

- `<id>` (positional) — Execution id

Extract structured data from a file (LLM for text, native parsers for binary)

- `--hint` (string) — Hint to the LLM extractor (text inputs only)


### `subkit files`

#### `subkit files download`

Download a file by id

- `<id>` (positional, required) — File id (fid_…)

- `--quiet` (default: false) — Suppress progress output

#### `subkit files get`

Show file metadata

- `<id>` (positional, required) — File id (fid_…)
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `subkit files link`

- `<fid>` (positional, required) — File id (fid_…)
- `--to` (string, required) — Owning resource as <resource_type>:<id>
- `--slug` (string) — Optional slug for the link
- `--role` (string) — Optional role for the link

#### `subkit files list`

List files

- `--status` (string) — Filter by status (pending|ready|failed|…)
- `--linked-to` (string) — Filter to files linked to <type>:<id> (e.g. conversation:abc-…)
- `--cursor` (string) — Pagination cursor
- `--limit` (string, default: 20) — Max rows (1-100)
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `subkit files patch`

Rename a file or change its description or category

- `<id>` (positional, required) — File id (fid_…)
- `--filename` (string) — New filename
- `--description` (string) — What it is for, in plain language — the assistant reads this to pick the right object. "" hands it back to automatic description.
- `--category` (string) — Catalog block, lowercase words joined by dashes (see `subkit categories list`). "" hands it back to automatic categorisation.
- `--json` — JSON-only output

#### `subkit files replace`

Replace a file's content (up to 5 MB); the id, reference and earlier versions stay

- `<id>` (positional, required) — File id (fid_…)
- `<path>` (positional, required) — Path to the new content
- `--content-type` (string) — Override detected MIME type
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `subkit files restore`

Make an earlier content version current again as a new version

- `<id>` (positional, required) — File id (fid_…)
- `<version>` (positional, required) — Version number to restore
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `subkit files stats`

Aggregate file counters for this tenant

- `--by` (string) — Group by: status|scanner_verdict (default: status)
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `subkit files upload`

Upload a file (inline ≤5 MB, authenticated streaming above)

- `<path>` (positional, required) — Path to file
- `--content-type` (string) — Override detected MIME type
- `--no-dedup` (default: false) — Skip the client-side sha256 dedup probe (forces an upload)
- `--link-to` (string) — After upload, link the file to <resource_type>:<id>
- `--slug` (string) — Optional slug for the link
- `--role` (string) — Optional role for the link
- `--label` (string) — Reserved for future labels (no-op today)
- `--quiet` (default: false) — Suppress progress output
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output (also silences progress)

#### `subkit files versions`

List a file's current and earlier content versions

- `<id>` (positional, required) — File id (fid_…)
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output


### `subkit health`

Runtime posture: liveness, token budget, failing runs, risk signals, schema drift, and process runtime. Use `subkit doctor` for connectivity/setup.

- `--window-hours` (string) — Lookback window for failing runs (default 24)
- `--json` — JSON output (composite object)


### `subkit hooks`

Manage inbound webhook bindings

#### `subkit hooks create`

Create an inbound webhook binding. The signing secret is read from a file (or - for stdin), never from an argument.

- `--slug` (string, required) — Public path: POST /v1/hooks/<slug>
- `--workflow-id` (string, required) — Workflow id to bind
- `--verifier` (string, default: standard) — Signature scheme: standard | github | stripe | hmac
- `--secret-file` (string, required) — File holding the shared signing secret (- reads stdin)
- `--config-file` (string) — JSON file for native_verifier_config, e.g. {"hmac": {...}} for the hmac verifier

#### `subkit hooks delete`

Delete an inbound webhook binding

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Hook id

#### `subkit hooks get`

Get an inbound webhook binding

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Hook id

#### `subkit hooks list`

List inbound webhook bindings

- `--json` — JSON output


### `subkit init`

Complete first-run engine bootstrap (consumes the token printed at engine boot)

- `--token` (string) — One-time bootstrap token printed by the engine on first boot
- `--engine-url` (string) — Engine base URL (defaults to http://localhost:3000)
- `--profile` (string) — Profile to write the new admin key into (default: default)
- `--admin-email` (string) — Admin user email (skip prompt)
- `--tenant-name` (string) — Tenant display name (skip prompt)
- `--llm-provider` (string) — LLM provider: mock|anthropic|openai|gemini|azure|bedrock|vertex (skip prompt)
- `--llm-api-key` (string) — LLM API key (skip prompt)
- `--llm-model` (string) — Model id the key is checked with and saved as llm.model (Azure: deployment name; needed for azure and bedrock)
- `--defaults` — Never prompt: fill anything still missing with local defaults (mock LLM provider, tenant 'Local', admin email from git config)

Upload a file as a knowledge source

- `--file` (string, required) — Path to file
- `--name` (string) — Source name (defaults to the filename)
- `--description` (string) — What it is for, in plain language — the assistant reads this to pick the right object. "" hands it back to automatic description.
- `--category` (string) — Catalog block, lowercase words joined by dashes (see `subkit categories list`). "" hands it back to automatic categorisation.
- `--tags` (string) — Comma-separated tags. When set, they are authoritative (no AI auto-tagging). Omit --description and --category to let the engine describe the source.
- `--scope` (string) — Scope: global | workflow
- `--workflow-id` (string) — Workflow id (required when scope=workflow)
- `--json` — JSON-only output (suppresses narration)

#### `subkit knowledge-sources delete`

Delete a knowledge source

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Knowledge source id

#### `subkit knowledge-sources get`

Get a knowledge source by id

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Knowledge source id

#### `subkit knowledge-sources history`

Show a knowledge source's content versions (newest first)

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Knowledge source id
- `--limit` (string) — Max rows
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `subkit knowledge-sources import`

Import a directory of markdown files as one knowledge source (upsert by slug; OKF-compatible frontmatter is read tolerantly)

- `<dir>` (positional, required) — Directory to import
- `--name` (string) — Source name (defaults to root index.md H1 or dirname)
- `--slug` (string) — Stable slug (defaults to slugified name)
- `--description` (string) — What it is for, in plain language — the assistant reads this to pick the right object. "" hands it back to automatic description.
- `--category` (string) — Catalog block, lowercase words joined by dashes (see `subkit categories list`). "" hands it back to automatic categorisation.
- `--tags` (string) — Comma-separated extra tags (frontmatter tags merge in)
- `--scope` (string) — Scope: global | workflow
- `--workflow-id` (string) — Workflow id (required when scope=workflow)
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `subkit knowledge-sources list`

List knowledge sources

- `--limit` (string, default: 20) — Max rows
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `subkit knowledge-sources patch`

Update a knowledge source

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Knowledge source id
- `--name` (string) — New name
- `--description` (string) — What it is for, in plain language — the assistant reads this to pick the right object. "" hands it back to automatic description.
- `--category` (string) — Catalog block, lowercase words joined by dashes (see `subkit categories list`). "" hands it back to automatic categorisation.
- `--tags` (string) — Comma-separated tags (replaces existing)
- `--status` (string) — Status: active | inactive

#### `subkit knowledge-sources restore`

Restore an earlier content version; the result is a new version

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Knowledge source id
- `--to` (string, required) — Version number from `subkit knowledge-sources history`
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `subkit knowledge-sources search`

Semantic search across knowledge sources

- `<query>` (positional, required) — Search query
- `--tags` (string) — Comma-separated tags to narrow results
- `--limit` (string, default: 10) — Max results
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output


### `subkit login`

Authenticate against a subkit engine

- `--engine-url` (string) — Engine base URL
- `--api-key` (string) — Scripted API-key login (skips device flow)
- `--tenant` (string) — Active tenant id
- `--profile` (string) — Profile name (~/.subkit/config.json)
- `--verbose` — Print each request with its trace id and timing to stderr (same as SUBKIT_DEBUG=1)
- `--portal-token` (string) — Authenticate as a portal-token principal


### `subkit logout`

Drop the active profile

- `--profile` (string) — Profile name to clear (default: active)


### `subkit logs`

Tail the engine's runtime log ring. --follow streams via SSE; --since accepts 5m / 2h / 1d / ISO-8601.

- `--engine-url` (string) — Engine base URL
- `--api-key` (string) — API key (audit:read required)
- `--profile` (string) — Use a named profile
- `--follow` (alias -f) — Live SSE tail (Ctrl-C to stop)
- `--since` (string) — Start time — relative (5m, 2h, 1d), ISO-8601, or unix-ms
- `--limit` (string) — Max entries when not following (default 200)
- `--module` (string) — Filter by module name (e.g. migrate, scheduler)
- `--action` (string) — Filter by action (e.g. drift_detected)
- `--level` (string) — Minimum level (trace|debug|info|warn|error|fatal)
- `--json` — Emit raw NDJSON for piping to jq, instead of pretty-printing


### `subkit ls`

List cached conversation sessions for the active profile

- `--limit` (string, default: 20) — Max rows
- `--search` (string) — Filter by substring in title / alias
- `--all` — Show every profile, not just the active one


### `subkit mcp`

Run a stdio MCP server proxied to the engine

- `--engine-url` (string) — Engine base URL
- `--api-key` (string) — API key (Bearer)
- `--tenant` (string) — Active tenant id
- `--profile` (string) — Profile name (~/.subkit/config.json)
- `--verbose` — Print each request with its trace id and timing to stderr (same as SUBKIT_DEBUG=1)

- `--limit` (string) — Max rows (<=500)
- `--json` — JSON output

### `subkit packages`

- `--out` (string, required) — Path of the archive to write
- `--only` (string) — Comma-separated kinds to export (connector_template, connector, file, skill, workflow, schedule, knowledge)
- `--category` (string) — Comma-separated catalog categories to export, one area per package
- `--json` — JSON output
- `--profile` (string) — Profile name
- `--engine-url` (string) — Engine base URL
- `--api-key` (string) — API key

#### `subkit packages import`

Import a package archive: shows the plan, asks for confirmation (--yes to skip), then applies exactly that plan

- `<file>` (positional, required) — Package archive (.zip)
- `--yes` — Apply without asking
- `--json` — JSON output
- `--profile` (string) — Profile name
- `--engine-url` (string) — Engine base URL
- `--api-key` (string) — API key

### `subkit schedules`

Scheduled workflow runs

- `--workflow` (string) — Filter by workflow id
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `subkit schedules create`

Schedule a workflow (a workflow carries at most one schedule; re-create updates it)

- `--workflow` (string, required) — Workflow id
- `--cron` (string, required) — 5-field cron or "every:<seconds>" (e.g. "0 8 * * *")
- `--timezone` (string) — IANA timezone (default UTC)
- `--executionMode` (string) — Connector environment: dev or prod (default: your setup default, otherwise dev)
- `--paused` (default: false) — Create in paused state
- `--input` (string) — JSON input payload passed to every run
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `subkit schedules delete`

Delete a schedule

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Schedule id
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `subkit schedules list`

List scheduled workflow runs

- `--workflow` (string) — Filter by workflow id
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `subkit schedules pause`

Pause a schedule (keeps the row)

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Schedule id
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `subkit schedules resume`

Resume a paused schedule

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Schedule id
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `subkit schedules update`

Update a schedule's cron, timezone, environment, or input

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Schedule id
- `--cron` (string) — New cron expression
- `--timezone` (string) — New IANA timezone
- `--executionMode` (string) — New connector environment: dev or prod
- `--input` (string) — New JSON input payload
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

### `subkit settings`

List, read, write, or interactively configure engine settings (secrets always masked)

#### `subkit settings configure`

Interactive Ink palette for inspecting settings (← / → cycles tabs, type to filter in Config, Enter to edit, Esc to exit). In non-TTY environments use --non-interactive to print the JSON contract instead.

- `--tab` (string) — Open directly on a tab: Status | Config | Usage | Skills | Knowledge
- `--non-interactive` — Skip the Ink renderer; print the GET /v1/settings response as JSON. Auto-detected when stdin is not a TTY.
- `--engine-url` (string) — Engine base URL
- `--api-key` (string) — API key
- `--profile` (string) — Profile name
- `--tenant` (string) — Tenant id (writes a tenant overlay)
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `subkit settings get`

Read one leaf by dotted path

- `<path>` (positional, required) — Setting path (e.g. llm.api_key)
- `--engine-url` (string) — Engine base URL
- `--api-key` (string) — API key
- `--profile` (string) — Profile name
- `--tenant` (string) — Tenant id (writes a tenant overlay)
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `subkit settings list`

List every leaf with its resolved value

- `--engine-url` (string) — Engine base URL
- `--api-key` (string) — API key
- `--profile` (string) — Profile name
- `--tenant` (string) — Tenant id (writes a tenant overlay)
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `subkit settings set`

Write one leaf. <value> must be valid JSON ('"abc"', 42, true, null).

- `<path>` (positional, required) — Setting path
- `<value>` (positional, required) — Value as JSON
- `--force` — Bypass requiresRestart guard in production
- `--engine-url` (string) — Engine base URL
- `--api-key` (string) — API key
- `--profile` (string) — Profile name
- `--tenant` (string) — Tenant id (writes a tenant overlay)
- `--json` — JSON output

### `subkit stats`

Tenant-scoped runtime statistics (needs stats:read)

#### `subkit stats chat`

Chat turns, modes, deduplication, and outcomes

- `--bucket` (string) — minute|hour|day|month|year
- `--from` (string) — ISO-8601 or relative (now-24h, now-7d, startOfMonth)
- `--to` (string) — ISO-8601 or relative (default: now)
- `--tz` (string) — IANA timezone (default UTC)
- `--group-by` (string) — comma-separated group dimensions (≤2)
- `--json` (default: false) — raw JSON output
- `--traffic-class` (string) — organic|synthetic|internal (comma-separated; default organic)
- `--operation` (string) — Filter canonical operation(s)
- `--outcome` (string) — Filter outcome(s)
- `--request-source` (string) — Filter request source(s)
- `--platform` (string) — Filter platform(s)
- `--response-mode` (string) — json|sse|sync|async|none

#### `subkit stats connectors`

Connector-call volume + latency + outcome. Example: subkit stats connectors --bucket hour --from now-24h

- `--bucket` (string) — minute|hour|day|month|year
- `--from` (string) — ISO-8601 or relative (now-24h, now-7d, startOfMonth)
- `--to` (string) — ISO-8601 or relative (default: now)
- `--tz` (string) — IANA timezone (default UTC)
- `--group-by` (string) — comma-separated group dimensions (≤2)
- `--json` (default: false) — raw JSON output
- `--connector-id` (string) — Filter by connector id
- `--connector-slug` (string) — Filter by connector slug
- `--driver` (string) — Filter by driver (comma-separated)
- `--method` (string) — Filter by method (comma-separated)
- `--outcome` (string) — Filter by outcome (success,denied,error)
- `--status-class` (string) — 2xx,3xx,4xx_other,4xx_auth,4xx_rate_limited,5xx,network_error,no_status
- `--include-endpoint` — Add normalized endpoint-path axis

#### `subkit stats conversations`

Conversation calls, streams, disconnects, and outcomes

- `--bucket` (string) — minute|hour|day|month|year
- `--from` (string) — ISO-8601 or relative (now-24h, now-7d, startOfMonth)
- `--to` (string) — ISO-8601 or relative (default: now)
- `--tz` (string) — IANA timezone (default UTC)
- `--group-by` (string) — comma-separated group dimensions (≤2)
- `--json` (default: false) — raw JSON output
- `--traffic-class` (string) — organic|synthetic|internal (comma-separated; default organic)
- `--operation` (string) — Filter canonical operation(s)
- `--outcome` (string) — Filter outcome(s)
- `--request-source` (string) — Filter request source(s)
- `--platform` (string) — Filter platform(s)
- `--response-mode` (string) — json|sse|sync|async|none

#### `subkit stats events`

Audit-event volume by class (webhook_outbound, webhook_inbound, chat, notification, schedule, self_healing, discovery, execution_lifecycle, policy, external_write). Example: subkit stats events --class self_healing --bucket day --from now-7d

- `--bucket` (string) — minute|hour|day|month|year
- `--from` (string) — ISO-8601 or relative (now-24h, now-7d, startOfMonth)
- `--to` (string) — ISO-8601 or relative (default: now)
- `--tz` (string) — IANA timezone (default UTC)
- `--group-by` (string) — comma-separated group dimensions (≤2)
- `--json` (default: false) — raw JSON output
- `--class` (string, required) — One of: webhook_outbound, webhook_inbound, chat, notification, schedule, self_healing, discovery, execution_lifecycle, policy, external_write
- `--outcome` (string) — Filter by outcome (success,denied,error)

#### `subkit stats executions`

Workflow run volume + duration distribution. Example: subkit stats executions --bucket hour --from now-24h

- `--bucket` (string) — minute|hour|day|month|year
- `--from` (string) — ISO-8601 or relative (now-24h, now-7d, startOfMonth)
- `--to` (string) — ISO-8601 or relative (default: now)
- `--tz` (string) — IANA timezone (default UTC)
- `--group-by` (string) — comma-separated group dimensions (≤2)
- `--json` (default: false) — raw JSON output
- `--workflow-id` (string) — Filter by workflow id
- `--status` (string) — Filter by status (comma-separated: succeeded,failed,…)
- `--request-source` (string) — Filter by request source (open set, e.g. api,scheduler,wait_reaper)
- `--execution-mode` (string) — dev|prod

#### `subkit stats http`

HTTP route volume, latency, bytes, and errors

- `--bucket` (string) — minute|hour|day|month|year
- `--from` (string) — ISO-8601 or relative (now-24h, now-7d, startOfMonth)
- `--to` (string) — ISO-8601 or relative (default: now)
- `--tz` (string) — IANA timezone (default UTC)
- `--group-by` (string) — comma-separated group dimensions (≤2)
- `--json` (default: false) — raw JSON output
- `--traffic-class` (string) — organic|synthetic|internal (comma-separated; default organic)
- `--operation` (string) — Filter canonical operation(s)
- `--outcome` (string) — Filter outcome(s)
- `--request-source` (string) — Filter request source(s)
- `--platform` (string) — Filter platform(s)
- `--response-mode` (string) — json|sse|sync|async|none

#### `subkit stats llm`

LLM token usage + cache-hit + latency. Example: subkit stats llm --bucket day --from startOfMonth

- `--bucket` (string) — minute|hour|day|month|year
- `--from` (string) — ISO-8601 or relative (now-24h, now-7d, startOfMonth)
- `--to` (string) — ISO-8601 or relative (default: now)
- `--tz` (string) — IANA timezone (default UTC)
- `--group-by` (string) — comma-separated group dimensions (≤2)
- `--json` (default: false) — raw JSON output
- `--model` (string) — Filter by model (comma-separated)
- `--flow` (string) — Filter by flow (comma-separated)
- `--user-id` (string) — Scope to one user (another user needs stats:read:all)
- `--mine` — Scope to your own usage (resolves your user id automatically)

#### `subkit stats mcp`

MCP JSON-RPC, sessions, capacity, tasks, and SSE

- `--bucket` (string) — minute|hour|day|month|year
- `--from` (string) — ISO-8601 or relative (now-24h, now-7d, startOfMonth)
- `--to` (string) — ISO-8601 or relative (default: now)
- `--tz` (string) — IANA timezone (default UTC)
- `--group-by` (string) — comma-separated group dimensions (≤2)
- `--json` (default: false) — raw JSON output
- `--traffic-class` (string) — organic|synthetic|internal (comma-separated; default organic)
- `--operation` (string) — Filter canonical operation(s)
- `--outcome` (string) — Filter outcome(s)
- `--request-source` (string) — Filter request source(s)
- `--platform` (string) — Filter platform(s)
- `--response-mode` (string) — json|sse|sync|async|none

#### `subkit stats operations`

The Overview's operations figures: runs, success rate, healthy connectors (now), applied repairs. Example: subkit stats operations --window 7d

- `--window` (string) — 24h (default), 7d or 30d
- `--from` (string) — Window start (ISO-8601 or now-24h, startOfMonth)
- `--to` (string) — Window end (default: now)
- `--json` — Emit the raw engine response


### `subkit status`

Print the active profile + engine reachability

- `--engine-url` (string) — Engine base URL
- `--api-key` (string) — API key (Bearer)
- `--tenant` (string) — Active tenant id
- `--profile` (string) — Profile name (~/.subkit/config.json)
- `--verbose` — Print each request with its trace id and timing to stderr (same as SUBKIT_DEBUG=1)


### `subkit subscriptions`

Manage event subscriptions

#### `subkit subscriptions create`

Create a subscription

- `--event-pattern` (string, required) — Event pattern to match, e.g. execution.* or execution.failed
- `--target-url` (string, required) — HTTPS URL that receives the signed delivery
- `--secret` (string, required) — Signing secret for deliveries
- `--active` (string) — Initial active state (true|false)

#### `subkit subscriptions delete`

Delete a subscription

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Subscription id

#### `subkit subscriptions deliveries`

List delivery attempts of a subscription, newest first

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Subscription id
- `--limit` (string) — Maximum number of deliveries (1-200, default 50)
- `--offset` (string) — Number of deliveries to skip
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `subkit subscriptions get`

Get a subscription

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Subscription id

#### `subkit subscriptions list`

List subscriptions

- `--json` — JSON output

#### `subkit subscriptions patch`

Update a subscription

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Subscription id
- `--event-pattern` (string) — New event pattern
- `--target-url` (string) — New target URL
- `--secret` (string) — New signing secret
- `--active` (string) — Set active state (true|false)

#### `subkit subscriptions replay`

Replay a subscription delivery

- `<sub-id>` (positional, required) — Subscription id
- `<delivery-id>` (positional, required) — Delivery id


### `subkit system`

Engine process operations (restart)

#### `subkit system restart`

Restart the engine so a saved restart-sensitive setting takes effect (needs a supervisor)

- `--wait` — Wait (up to 240 s) until the restarted engine runs the saved settings
- `--engine-url` (string) — Engine base URL
- `--api-key` (string) — API key
- `--profile` (string) — Profile name
- `--json` — JSON output


### `subkit system-accounts`

Manage system accounts

#### `subkit system-accounts create`

Create a system account

- `--name` (string, required) — Account name

#### `subkit system-accounts delete`

Delete a system account

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Account id

#### `subkit system-accounts list`

List system accounts

- `--json` — JSON output


### `subkit tasks`

Tasks: a goal with limits that works on its own and asks before it acts

- `--category` (string) — Only this catalog block
- `--archived` (default: false) — Show archived tasks instead
- `--limit` (string, default: 50) — Max rows
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `subkit tasks abort`

Stop a run that is running, waiting or sleeping

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Run id (see `subkit tasks runs <id>`)
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `subkit tasks create`

Create a task from a JSON file (--file); it belongs to you and starts by hand until a person allows scheduled runs in the Cockpit

- `--file` (string, required) — Path to the task JSON file
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `subkit tasks delete`

Delete a task: it is archived, its open run stops and its standing permission ends

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Task id
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `subkit tasks get`

Show a task, its latest run and whether its standing permission is live

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Task id
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `subkit tasks list`

List tasks (your own; an admin sees all)

- `--category` (string) — Only this catalog block
- `--archived` (default: false) — Show archived tasks instead
- `--limit` (string, default: 50) — Max rows
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `subkit tasks pause`

Pause a task: no run starts and an open run sleeps until you resume it

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Task id
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `subkit tasks resume`

Resume a paused task; a run that slept through the pause continues

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Task id
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `subkit tasks run`

Start a task now, as you; the run works in its own conversation

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Task id
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `subkit tasks runs`

List the runs of a task, newest first

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Task id
- `--limit` (string, default: 20) — Max rows
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `subkit tasks update`

Replace a task from a JSON file (--file) or change only its schedule (--cron with --timezone, or --run-at); a content change stops the open run and ends the standing permission

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Task id
- `--file` (string) — Path to the task JSON file
- `--cron` (string) — New 5-field cron (e.g. "0 8 * * 1-5")
- `--timezone` (string) — New IANA timezone (default UTC)
- `--run-at` (string) — Run once at this ISO instant (e.g. 2026-12-01T07:00:00+01:00)
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output


### `subkit tenants`

List tenants you belong to or switch the active one

- `--engine-url` (string) — Engine base URL
- `--api-key` (string) — API key (Bearer)
- `--tenant` (string) — Active tenant id
- `--profile` (string) — Profile name (~/.subkit/config.json)
- `--verbose` — Print each request with its trace id and timing to stderr (same as SUBKIT_DEBUG=1)
- `<use>` (positional) — Tenant id to switch to


### `subkit update`

Update the subkit CLI to the latest release, or to the version of your engine

- `--check` (default: false) — Report whether an update exists without installing it
- `--force` (default: false) — Download and install even when already up to date
- `--match-engine` (default: false) — Install the version the engine of the active profile runs
- `--rollback` (default: false) — Restore the most recently retained subkit binary
- `--to` (string) — With --rollback, the retained version to restore (default: the most recent)


### `subkit users`

Manage identity users

#### `subkit users create`

Create a user in the caller's tenant

- `--email` (string, required) — User email
- `--role` (string) — Role: admin|member|enduser (default member)
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `subkit users delete`

Delete a user

- `<id>` (positional, required) — User id

#### `subkit users get`

Fetch a user by id

- `<id>` (positional, required) — User id

#### `subkit users invite`

Issue a single-use provisioning invite for a user (token shown once)

- `<id>` (positional, required) — User id to invite
- `--scopes` (string) — Comma-separated scope strings (default: your own credential's scopes; ["*"] only when your credential has no scope limits)
- `--allowed-workflows` (string) — Comma-separated workflow ids/slugs
- `--allowed-connectors` (string) — Comma-separated connector ids/slugs
- `--ttl` (string) — Invite lifetime in minutes
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `subkit users list`

List identity users

- `--limit` (string) — Max rows
- `--app` (string) — Only users who signed in to this app (product_id, see subkit apps list)
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `subkit users patch`

Update a user's role (admin only)

- `<id>` (positional, required) — User id
- `--role` (string, required) — New role: admin|member|enduser


### `subkit vault`

The vault (Tresor): secrets, logins and connector credentials. Workflows name an item as ${secret.<name>}; values never reach the model.

#### `subkit vault add`

Add a secret or a login. The token or password is read from stdin or a hidden prompt, never from arguments.

- `<name>` (positional, required) — Handle name, e.g. crm-token
- `--kind` (string, default: secret) — secret | login
- `--username` (string) — login: the username
- `--scope` (string, default: workspace) — workspace | person
- `--env` (string, default: prod) — dev | prod
- `--description` (string) — What the item is for
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `subkit vault attach`

Attach a connector's credential as a vault item. Name the connector by slug or id and choose its record with --env; each environment keeps its own credential. The secret comes from stdin or a hidden prompt, never from arguments: the token, the header or query value, the password, the PEM key, or for aws_sigv4 the secret access key and an optional session token on a second line.

- `<connector-id>` (positional, required) — Connector slug or id
- `--env` (string) — dev | prod: the connector record to attach to; required when the slug has both
- `--mode` (string) — bearer | header | query | basic | aws_sigv4 | signed_jwt | none (default: the connector's auth type)
- `--header` (string) — header mode: the header name; without it stdin holds Name=Value lines
- `--query` (string) — query mode: the parameter name; without it stdin holds name=value lines
- `--username` (string) — basic mode username
- `--access-key-id` (string) — aws_sigv4 access key id
- `--skip-checks` — Skip the post-set connectivity probe
- `--json` — JSON-only output

#### `subkit vault connector`

List the vault items of one connector

- `<connector-id>` (positional, required) — Connector id
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `subkit vault list`

List vault items: names and metadata, never values

- `--scope` (string) — workspace | person
- `--kind` (string) — connector | secret | login | template_client
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `subkit vault refresh`

Refresh the OAuth token of a connector's vault item

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Vault item id

#### `subkit vault reveal`

Print a vault item's value. Every reveal is recorded in the audit log.

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Vault item id
- `--field` (string) — Print only this field
- `--yes` — Confirm that the value may appear in this terminal

#### `subkit vault rm`

Delete a vault item and its value

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Vault item id

#### `subkit vault rotate`

Replace the value of a secret or login. The new value is read from stdin.

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Vault item id
- `--username` (string) — login: a new username

#### `subkit vault show`

Show one vault item's metadata and activity

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Vault item id
- `--json` — JSON output


### `subkit workflows`

Manage workflows

#### `subkit workflows create`

Create a workflow from a JSON file (--file) or a solution recipe (--from-recipe <slug>, see `subkit connector-templates recipe-pack solutions`). Runs `validate` and `preview` by default; pass --skip-checks to bypass.

- `--file` (string) — Path to WorkflowDef JSON
- `--from-recipe` (string) — Slug of a solution recipe; its connectors are bound to the ones you already have
- `--bind` (string) — With --from-recipe: bind connectors yourself, as <template or placeholder>=<connector id or slug>[,…]; needed for templates without a fixed address such as http
- `--environment` (string, default: dev) — Where the pre-flight preview runs: dev (default) or prod. Use the environment the workflow's schedule or webhook runs in; writes stay held either way.
- `--skip-checks` — Skip the validate+preview pre-flight entirely (NOT recommended). Preview warnings never block; only validation errors and preview failures do.
- `--input` (string) — Input JSON string passed to the preview dry-run. With --from-recipe it defaults to the recipe's sample input.
- `--json` — JSON-only output (suppresses narration)

#### `subkit workflows delete`

Delete a workflow

- `<id>` (positional) — Workflow id

#### `subkit workflows dry-run`

Preview a draft WorkflowDef by dry-running it via runExecution (source=draft). No persistence. Alias: dry-run.

- `<file>` (positional, required) — Path to WorkflowDef JSON
- `--input` (string) — Input JSON string
- `--name` (string) — Optional label (goes to executions.source_ref)
- `--environment` (string, default: dev) — Where the run executes: dev (default) or prod. Sent as the x-subkit-environment header; write steps need a connector bound to this environment.

#### `subkit workflows get`

Get a workflow by id

- `<id>` (positional) — Workflow id

#### `subkit workflows history`

List committed versions of a workflow

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Workflow id
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `subkit workflows invoke-snippet`

Emit a ready-to-paste, authenticated snippet to run a saved workflow from your own app or CI (curl/node/python).

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Workflow id
- `--lang` (string, default: curl) — Snippet language: curl (default), node, or python
- `--environment` (string, default: prod) — Where the call runs: prod (default) or dev. Printed as the x-subkit-environment header.
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `subkit workflows list`

List workflows, grouped into catalog blocks

- `--limit` (string, default: 50) — Max rows
- `--category` (string) — Only this catalog block
- `--connector` (string) — Only workflows using this connector (id or slug)
- `--flat` — One flat table instead of grouped blocks
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `subkit workflows patch`

Change a workflow's name, description or category without saving a new version (the slug and its wf_<slug> tool stay as they are).

- `<workflow>` (positional, required) — Workflow id or slug
- `--name` (string) — New display name
- `--description` (string) — What it is for, in plain language — the assistant reads this to pick the right object. "" hands it back to automatic description.
- `--category` (string) — Catalog block, lowercase words joined by dashes (see `subkit categories list`). "" hands it back to automatic categorisation.
- `--json` — JSON-only output (suppresses narration)

#### `subkit workflows preview`

Preview a draft WorkflowDef by dry-running it via runExecution (source=draft). No persistence. Alias: dry-run.

- `<file>` (positional, required) — Path to WorkflowDef JSON
- `--input` (string) — Input JSON string
- `--name` (string) — Optional label (goes to executions.source_ref)
- `--environment` (string, default: dev) — Where the run executes: dev (default) or prod. Sent as the x-subkit-environment header; write steps need a connector bound to this environment.

#### `subkit workflows restore`

Restore a prior workflow version

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Workflow id
- `<version>` (positional, required) — Version number

#### `subkit workflows run`

Run a saved workflow, an inline draft definition, or a single step

- `<id>` (positional) — Workflow id or slug (omit when using --draft or --step)
- `--input` (string) — Input JSON string. Prefix with `@` to read from a file (e.g. `--input @./payload.json`).
- `--input-file` (string) — Upload a file and substitute its ref into --input at key K. Format: K=<path>. Repeatable.
- `--draft` (string) — Path to a draft WorkflowDef JSON file (no commit)
- `--step` (string) — Path to a single StepDef JSON file (no workflow persistence)
- `--name` (string) — Optional label for --draft runs (goes to executions.source_ref)
- `--slug` (string) — Optional workflow_slug for --step runs (cosmetic)
- `--follow` — Queue the run and stream its progress live (step-by-step JSON lines). Saved workflows only.
- `--idempotency-key` (string) — Make this trigger safe to repeat: a second run with the same key is not started, the first run's id comes back instead. Saved workflows only.
- `--environment` (string, default: dev) — Where the run executes: dev (default) or prod. Sent as the x-subkit-environment header; write steps need a connector bound to this environment.

#### `subkit workflows update`

Update a workflow from a JSON file (PUT the full definition). Runs `validate` and `preview` by default; pass --skip-checks to bypass. An unchanged definition does not rotate a version.

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Workflow id
- `--file` (string, required) — Path to WorkflowDef JSON
- `--environment` (string, default: dev) — Where the pre-flight preview runs: dev (default) or prod. Use the environment the workflow's schedule or webhook runs in; writes stay held either way.
- `--skip-checks` — Skip the validate+preview pre-flight entirely (NOT recommended). Preview warnings never block; only validation errors and preview failures do.
- `--input` (string) — Input JSON string passed to the preview dry-run.
- `--json` — JSON-only output (suppresses narration)

#### `subkit workflows validate`

Validate a draft WorkflowDef JSON file (structural + step schema checks). No execution, no persistence.

- `<file>` (positional, required) — Path to WorkflowDef JSON

<!-- Source: settings.md -->

# SubKit runtime settings

Look up every runtime setting with its description and default value.
You change a value with `subkit settings configure` and `subkit settings set`, through the
HTTP or MCP settings APIs, or in the canonical config file. Per-tenant overrides go
into the file's `tenants` section and only apply to settings tagged `scope=tenant`.

A value resolves in this order: tenant overlay, then global value, then schema
default. Environment variables never set a runtime setting; only the bootstrap-only
process bindings `database.url`, `storage.backend`, `storage.filesystem.root` and
`deployment.mode` (from `SUBKIT_DEPLOYMENT_MODE`) come from the environment at startup.

## log
Logging

| path | type | default | scope | sensitive | requiresRestart | description |
| ---- | ---- | ------- | ----- | --------- | --------------- | ----------- |
| `log.format` | enum("dev" \| "pretty" \| "prod" \| "ndjson" \| "json") | `"ndjson"` | global | no | no | Log output format |
| `log.level` | enum("trace" \| "debug" \| "info" \| "warn" \| "error" \| "fatal") | `"info"` | global | no | no | Log verbosity |

## deployment
Deployment

| path | type | default | scope | sensitive | requiresRestart | description |
| ---- | ---- | ------- | ----- | --------- | --------------- | ----------- |
| `deployment.mode` | enum("server" \| "local_workspace") | `"server"` | global | no | yes | Bootstrap-only deployment mode: server, or local_workspace when SubKit Desktop runs the engine on this device (loopback only, local sign-in, laptop profile). Set SUBKIT_DEPLOYMENT_MODE and restart. |

## server
HTTP server

| path | type | default | scope | sensitive | requiresRestart | description |
| ---- | ---- | ------- | ----- | --------- | --------------- | ----------- |
| `server.desktop_dev_callback` | boolean | `false` | global | no | no | Also accept subkit-dev://callback as a sign-in target, for development builds of SubKit Desktop. Outside NODE_ENV=production it is accepted without this setting. |
| `server.desktop_min_version` | string | `"0.1.0"` | global | no | no | Oldest SubKit Desktop version this engine accepts. Published as clients.desktop.min_version in /.well-known/service-descriptor.json; an older app asks for an update instead of signing in. |
| `server.hosted_rate_limit.global_per_minute` | number | `0` | global | no | no | Operator request ceiling across hosted ingress per minute; zero denies hosted ingress |
| `server.hosted_rate_limit.peer_per_minute` | number | `0` | global | no | no | Operator request ceiling per verified connection peer and minute; zero denies hosted ingress |
| `server.hosted_rate_limit.principal_per_minute` | number | `0` | global | no | no | Operator request ceiling per authenticated principal and tenant per minute; zero denies hosted requests |
| `server.hosted_rate_limit.tenant_per_minute` | number | `0` | global | no | no | Operator request ceiling per hosted tenant and minute; zero denies hosted requests |
| `server.hosted_rate_limit.tenant_per_month` | number | `0` | global | no | no | Operator request allowance per hosted tenant and UTC calendar month; zero denies hosted requests |
| `server.port` | number | `3000` | global | no | yes | HTTP port to bind (1..65535) |
| `server.public_base_url` | string | `""` | global | no | no | External-facing URL the engine resolves at. Used by /install, chat link replies, and OAuth2 redirect-URI synthesis. Required for any OAuth2 connector. |
| `server.restart_supervised` | boolean | `false` | global | no | no | A supervisor (systemd with Restart=on-failure, Docker with a restart policy) starts the engine again after it ends. Enables POST /v1/system/restart (exit code 75). |
| `server.root_redirect_to_cockpit` | boolean | `true` | global | no | no | Send a browser that opens / to the Cockpit at /cockpit. Agents keep the Markdown index. Set false to show browsers the engine index at /; it stays at /engine either way. |
| `server.trusted_proxy_hops` | number | `0` | global | no | no | Trusted reverse-proxy hops counted from the right of X-Forwarded-For; zero ignores forwarding headers. |
| `server.trusted_proxy_ips` | array | `[]` | global | no | no | Exact trusted reverse-proxy socket peer IPs. Every configured forwarding hop must match; X-Real-IP is never trusted. |

## database
Database connection

| path | type | default | scope | sensitive | requiresRestart | description |
| ---- | ---- | ------- | ----- | --------- | --------------- | ----------- |
| `database.connect_timeout_ms` | number | `10000` | global | no | yes | Deadline for acquiring or establishing a PostgreSQL connection. |
| `database.idle_timeout_ms` | number | `30000` | global | no | yes | Time before an unused pooled connection is closed. |
| `database.keepalive_delay_ms` | number | `10000` | global | no | yes | Initial TCP keepalive delay for PostgreSQL connections. |
| `database.pool_max` | number | `10` | global | no | yes | Maximum application connections per pool and replica. |
| `database.query_timeout_ms` | number | `150000` | global | no | yes | Client-side PostgreSQL query deadline in milliseconds. |
| `database.statement_timeout_ms` | number | `120000` | global | no | yes | Server-side PostgreSQL statement deadline, initialized on each session. |
| `database.url` | string | `—` | global | yes | yes | Bootstrap-only Postgres connection string. Rotate DATABASE_URL and restart replicas; runtime revisions cannot change this binding. |

## llm
LLM configuration

| path | type | default | scope | sensitive | requiresRestart | description |
| ---- | ---- | ------- | ----- | --------- | --------------- | ----------- |
| `llm.api_key` | string | `""` | tenant | yes | no | Primary LLM API key |
| `llm.context_1m` | boolean | `false` | tenant | no | no | Enable 1M context window where supported |
| `llm.critic.enabled` | boolean | `false` | tenant | no | no | Run the second-stage LLM critic on workflow drafts after every static gate passes |
| `llm.critic.max_consecutive_rejections` | number | `3` | tenant | no | no | After this many consecutive critic_rejected results in a conversation, skip the critic to avoid an infinite re-author loop |
| `llm.critic.min_steps` | number | `3` | tenant | no | no | Minimum step count for the critic to run on a draft (drift in recent drafts also triggers a run) |
| `llm.fallback_model` | string | `""` | tenant | no | no | Fallback model identifier |
| `llm.fallback_provider` | enum("mock" \| "anthropic" \| "openai" \| "gemini" \| "azure" \| "bedrock" \| "vertex" \| "ai_gateway") | `null` | tenant | no | no | Fallback provider on primary failure |
| `llm.model` | string | `""` | tenant | no | no | Primary model identifier |
| `llm.output_guard` | enum("soft" \| "hard" \| "off") | `"soft"` | global | no | no | LLM output safety mode (soft: rewrite + log, hard: throw, off: bypass — never use in production) |
| `llm.provider` | enum("mock" \| "anthropic" \| "openai" \| "gemini" \| "azure" \| "bedrock" \| "vertex" \| "ai_gateway") | `"mock"` | tenant | no | no | Primary LLM provider |

| `llm.providers.anthropic.base_url` | string | `""` | global | no | no | Optional base URL override |
| `llm.providers.anthropic.model` | string | `""` | tenant | no | no | Default model identifier |
| `llm.providers.azure.api_key` | string | `""` | tenant | yes | no |  |

| `llm.providers.azure.resource_name` | string | `""` | global | no | no |  |
| `llm.providers.azure.use_deployment_based_urls` | boolean | `false` | global | no | no |  |
| `llm.providers.bedrock.access_key_id` | string | `""` | global | yes | no |  |
| `llm.providers.bedrock.base_url` | string | `""` | global | no | no |  |
| `llm.providers.bedrock.model` | string | `""` | tenant | no | no |  |

## Workspace settings

Every workspace keeps its own name, time zone and language. They are not runtime settings: the workspace owner or a holder of `identity:write` changes them in the Cockpit under Settings › Workspace or with `PATCH /v1/identity/workspace`.

| field | type | default | description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `display_name` | string | `—` | Name of the workspace |
| `timezone` | string | `"UTC"` | IANA time zone, e.g. Europe/Berlin |
| `language` | enum("de" \| "en") | `"en"` | Language for texts that no person's language decides, such as device connector names and scheduled task runs; a person's own app language still wins |

Texts that no person's language decides follow the workspace language: device connector names when the desktop app sends no known language, and new tasks created without a language from the request. A person's own app language still wins; without either, the text is English.

## Authentication providers

`auth.providers` is one atomic, validated runtime setting available through Cockpit, HTTP, MCP, `subkit settings`, and the canonical config file. Records use `protocol: api_key` or `oidc`; one API-key adapter and multiple named direct OIDC adapters may coexist. Provider ids must be unique, and every OIDC callback is `/v1/identity/login/callback` on `server.public_base_url`. A successful write is active for subsequent browser-login requests without an engine restart.

OIDC records are public clients using Authorization Code with PKCE. Runtime configuration intentionally has no `client_secret` field and rejects one if supplied; use an issuer that supports public clients with `token_endpoint_auth_method=none`. The environment is not an auth-provider source.

Configured labels are diagnostic metadata only. The common `mcp-auth` surface derives its two user actions from protocol and always presents `Continue with SSO` before `Continue with API key`. Discovery exposes the canonical labels `SSO` and `API key`; no provider-specific route or parallel configuration tree is accepted.

## Filesystem object store

On a single device, the engine can keep files and offloaded results in a folder instead of an S3-compatible object store. Set two environment variables before the engine starts:

| Variable | Setting | Value |
| -------- | ------- | ----- |
| `OBJECT_STORAGE_BACKEND` | `storage.backend` | `filesystem` (default `s3`) |
| `OBJECT_STORAGE_ROOT` | `storage.filesystem.root` | absolute folder, for example `<app data>/local/<workspace>/files` |

Both are bootstrap-only: they come from the environment on every start, a stored revision cannot change them, and the settings APIs refuse to write them. The `storage.object_store` values are not needed in this mode.

- **Startup check:** the parent folder must exist. The engine creates the folder with mode `0700`, tightens an existing one to `0700`, and proves it can write, read, delete and hard-link inside it. If a check fails, the engine does not start and names the reason (`root_parent_missing`, `root_not_directory`, `root_not_writable`, `root_cross_device`, `root_no_hard_links`) with a remedy.
- **Writes:** each object is written to a staging file, flushed to disk, then linked into place, so a reader sees the whole object or nothing. An existing key is never overwritten. Files get mode `0600`, folders `0700`.
- **Keys:** every key segment is encoded to lowercase ASCII (`a-z`, `0-9`, `.`, `_`, `-`, other bytes as `%xx`), so keys that differ only in case or Unicode form stay apart on case-insensitive disks, and Windows reserved names are safe. `..`, empty segments and absolute keys are refused, and a link that leads outside the folder is never followed.
- **Backup:** the folder is the whole object store; copy it together with the database dump.
- **Not supported:** network drives, cloud-synced folders and disks without hard links, such as exFAT.

<!-- Source: connectors.md -->

# Connector & recipe catalog

Find the connector templates and recipes that ship with SubKit. There are **61 connector templates** in **16 categories**, carrying **248 recipes**: complete, runnable workflows you clone instead of starting from a blank page.

A **template** connects a system: base URL, sign-in flow, endpoint schema and a vendor-basics skill. A **recipe** is a complete workflow built on that template. Say what you want in a conversation, and SubKit clones the closest recipe as your first draft.

| -------- | ---- | ------ | ---- | ---------------- |
| **HubSpot** | `hubspot` | http | bearer | HubSpot CRM API |
| **Salesforce** | `salesforce` | http | oauth2 | Salesforce REST API |

### Payments

| -------- | ---- | ------ | ---- | ---------------- |

### E-commerce

| -------- | ---- | ------ | ---- | ---------------- |

## Recipes

Grouped by template. **Trigger** is how the workflow starts: `request` (on demand — chat, CLI, MCP, REST), `schedule` (cron), or `webhook` (an external system calls in). **Also uses** lists connectors beyond the template's own.

### Airtable (`airtable`)

| Recipe | What it does | Trigger | Also uses |
| ------ | ------------ | ------- | --------- |
| `create-record` | POST a new row with fields. | request | — |
| `delete-record` | DELETE a record by id. | request | — |
| `get-record` | Fetch a single record from a table. | request | — |
| `list-bases` | Enumerate accessible bases via the meta API. | request | — |
| `list-records` | Page through records with offset-based pagination. | request | — |
| `list-records-formula` | Run a server-side filter formula against a table. | request | — |
| `list-tables` | Enumerate tables (and their fields) in a base. | request | — |
| `update-record` | PATCH a record's fields (partial update). | request | — |

<!-- Source: transactional-email.md -->

# Reply by email to a signed request

Someone sends a request through your form, for example for access, and should get a confirmation by email: exactly one, and only to their own address.
This chapter shows developers how a workflow sends that reply as plain text through Gmail.
Afterwards, SubKit checks origin, approval and recipient before every send, and a request sent twice produces no second email.

Signed means: your website or backend computes a checksum over the request with a secret key.
SubKit recomputes it and starts nothing if it does not match.
A person reviews sender, template and limits before anything is sent.

The path is always the same: **signed request → reviewed workflow → approval → one reply**.

### What you need

- A Gmail connection (connector) in your workspace.
- A signed source, that is your form backend, which sends requests in the Standard Webhooks format. Standard Webhooks is an open format for signed HTTP messages.
- A person who approves the workflow.
- An operator who reviews the workflow before activation.

Never skip signature verification.
Never use a public API key or credentials from the browser for the source.

### Set up the workflow

1. Set `execution_privacy: sensitive` and a strict input schema with bounded lengths.
2. Add exactly one plain-text Gmail send step. Its request body contains only `raw`.
3. Keep sender, connection and template in the workflow. The request selects only the reviewed original recipient.
4. On the Gmail request step, add the `transactional_delivery` profile and `max_retries: 0`.
5. Set `max_body_bytes` from the bounded template, not the largest allowed value.

The signed JSON body must contain the request UUID and the event type.
Input paths start at `body`.
For a body with `event`, `reference` and `contact.address`, the profile looks like this:

```json
{
  "kind": "gmail_transactional",
  "webhook_id": "<reviewed-binding-uuid>",
  "event_type": "registration.requested",
  "event_type_input": "body.event",
  "request_id_input": "body.reference",
  "recipient_input": "body.contact.address",
  "from": "sender@example.test",
  "content_type": "text/plain",
  "max_body_bytes": 8192
}
```

`max_body_bytes` counts the finished Gmail JSON, including the extra size from base64.
This step cannot read page by page and cannot spread to several recipients. It also does not support a second fixed-recipient profile or response filtering.

You can also describe this workflow in the Cockpit chat. The chat knows this profile and its limits.

### Bind and review

1. In the same workspace, create an active Standard Webhooks binding for the workflow. The binding links the source to the workflow. Use exactly the reviewed event type and its own signing secret.
2. In the source, save the request UUID and the original payload before sending.
3. Send the UUID in the signed body and in `webhook-id`.
4. Ask an operator to review version, sender, connection, signed source, field paths, byte limit and run limits.
5. Activate the workflow and approve it.

### Test the reply

1. Send a test request to a controlled recipient.
2. Check that the signed source still exists after activation.
3. Connect the public form.
4. Send the same request twice and check that one message arrives.

### Compute the signature

Your source signs each request with HMAC-SHA256, a checksum with a secret key.
Use the secret verbatim as the UTF-8 key. SubKit does not strip a `whsec_` prefix and does not Base64-decode the key.

1. Compute HMAC-SHA256 over `id.timestamp.rawBody`.
2. Base64-encode the result.
3. Send `webhook-signature: v1,<base64>`.

Also send matching timestamp and event-type headers.
The header alone is unsigned. So the event type must also match the reviewed field in the signed body.

### What happens next

Before sending, the engine checks the approval, the signed source and the recipient again.
It refuses CC, BCC and extra recipients.

Good to know:

- A failed or unclear send is never resent automatically. There is no retry or reset operation.
- Each original request gets at most one reply, across workflow versions and runs.
- A signature only confirms where the request comes from. Only the approval allows the workflow to send.
- A retried handoff keeps the same payload and ID and renews only timestamp and signature. Changed content under the same ID is refused.

### Send one email per queued message

Sometimes the source cannot send a webhook, for example because its server may not open outbound connections.
Then it puts messages into a queue, and a scheduled workflow picks them up with `outbox_delivery`.
An earlier fixed, read-only `GET` step returns the next queue entry. The email step declares `{kind: "gmail_outbox", source_step_id, recipient_field, item_id_field, from, content_type: "text/plain", max_body_bytes, max_per_day}`. Use `execution_privacy: sensitive` and `max_retries: 0`.

- The recipient comes only from that queue response in the same run. The engine compares it with the message before sending.
- Each queue entry gets at most one attempt, across workflow versions and runs. An unclear result is never resent automatically.
- `max_per_day` caps the messages within any 24 hours.
- Whoever can fill the queue chooses the recipients. Approve only a queue you trust; the approval dialog names it.

### Inspect outcomes

`GET /v1/workflows/{id}/transactional-mail-receipts?limit=20&offset=0` requires `workflow:read` for that workflow.

It returns:

- Request, run and step IDs
- State and timestamps

It does not return the applicant's address or the message content.

The audit log records when a send was reserved and how it ended.

| State | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `sent` | Gmail answered with a message ID. This confirms that Gmail accepted it, not that it reached the inbox. |
| `attempted`, `delivery_unknown` | The operator inspects the case. |

### If something does not work

| What you see | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| The state is `attempted` or `delivery_unknown` | The operator inspects the case. There is no automatic resend and no reset endpoint. |
| A request is refused although the signature is correct | Check that the event type in the signed body matches the header and the reviewed field path, and that the UUID in the body and in `webhook-id` agree. |
| A repeated handoff is refused | The content under that signed ID changed. Send the same payload and ID again and renew only timestamp and signature. |
| Sending is refused because of recipient headers | Remove CC, BCC and extra recipient headers. Only the reviewed original recipient is allowed. |
| The signed source is gone after activation | Create a new binding and activate a reviewed workflow version that references its actual ID. |
